STUDYQURAN:50:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:intro/r7.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:50:intro/r7.claim: The Prophet is also reported to recite Qaf and al-Qamar at both feasts and often during the morning prayer.
STUDYQURAN:50:intro/r7.anchor: read Qāf and Sūrah 54, al-Qamar, during the

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p28/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p28/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p28/r6.claim: After mentioning the destruction of earlier peoples and calling this a warning, the text says the warned event is near: the approaching event is the Resurrection, also called near in 54:1.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p28/r6.anchor: أزفت الآزفة: أي قربت الموصوفة بالقرب في قوله: اقتربت الساعة

RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r1.claim: The sūra opens by repeating and supporting the previous sūra’s closing announcement that the Imminent Event has drawn near.
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r1.anchor: أول السورة مناسب لآخر ما قبلها ، وهو قوله : { أزفت الازفة } ( النجم : 57 ) فكأنه أعاد ذلك مع الدليل

RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r2.speaker: المفسرون بأسرهم
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r2.claim: All exegetes take the wording as an actual past splitting of the moon, supported by reports about the event.
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r2.anchor: والمفسرون بأسرهم على أن المراد أن القمر انشق ، وحصل فيه الانشقاق ، ودلت الأخبار على حديث الانشقاق

RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r3.speaker: جمع من الصحابة
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r3.claim: A famous report in the Ṣaḥīḥ, transmitted by a group of Companions, says the Prophet was asked for the splitting itself as a sign, prayed to God, and the moon split; al-Rāzī cites it as sound.
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r3.anchor: وفي الصحيح خبر مشهور رواه جمع من الصحابة ، وقالوا : سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آية الانشقاق بعينها معجزة

RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r4.claim: Some exegetes take the verse to mean that the moon will split in the future; al-Rāzī calls this far-fetched and unnecessary, since opponents of cosmic rupture reject both past and future occurrence, while its proponents need no reinterpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r4.anchor: وقال بعض الفسرين المراد سينشق ، وهو بعيد ولا معنى له

RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r5.claim: The objection that such a momentous event should have been universally transmitted is answered by the Quran’s lasting miraculous status: scholars did not need another miracle as proof.
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r5.anchor: فكان القرآن معجزة باقية إلى قيام القيامة لا يتمسك بمعجزة أخرى فلم ينقله العلماء بحيث يبلغ حد التواتر

RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r6.claim: Historians omitted the event because chronicle writers were often astrologers, who explained it away as a lunar eclipse or an atmospheric image of half a moon elsewhere.
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r6.anchor: وأما المؤرخون فتركوه ، لأن التواريخ في أكثر الأمر يستعملها المنجم ، وهو لما وقع الأمر قالوا : بأنه مثل خسوف القمر

RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r7.claim: The Quran is the strongest proof, and the event must be believed because the truthful Prophet reported it; denying cosmic rupture and restoration is an ignoble argument, since such changes to the heavens are possible.
RAZI-FULL:v29p26/r7.anchor: والقرآن أدل دليل وأقوى مثبت له ، وإمكانه لا يشك فيه ، وقد أخبر عنه الصادق فيجب اعتقاد وقوعه

STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r1.claim: Most commentators classify the sūrah as Makkan; some classify verse 45 or verses 44–46 as Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r1.anchor: ost commentators maintain that al-Qamar is a Makkan

STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r2.claim: The sūrah is named for the moon mentioned in verse 1 and is also known by its opening words, Iqtarabat al-sāʿah.
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r2.anchor: It takes its name from the mention of the moon in the first verse and is also known by its first words, Iqtarabat al-sāʿah

STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r3.speaker: Āl, Sy
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r3.claim: The opening reiterates 53:57, and the destruction stories expand on the previous sūrah’s references to ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Noah.
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r3.anchor: This sūrah follows thematically upon the previous sūrah in that the first verse reiterates 53:57, The imminent is nigh

STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r4.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r4.claim: The Prophet reportedly recited Sūrah 50 and al-Qamar at both Eid prayers and other major prayer gatherings.
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r4.anchor: It is reported that the Prophet would recite Qāf

STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r5.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r5.claim: Most commentators understand the first two verses as the Prophet’s miracle: at Minā, after disbelievers demanded a sign, he pointed to the moon, which split in two around Mount Ḥirāʾ; he called them to witness and the division vanished.
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r5.anchor: The first two verses of al-Qamar are understood by the vast majority of commentators as a reference to a miracle performed by the Prophet.

STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r7.claim: The sūrah warns the Prophet’s opponents of Judgment, recounts earlier peoples overthrown for similar offenses, then moves from punishment to divine decree and accounting and ends with the reverent’s reward.
STUDYQURAN:54:intro/r7.anchor: After warning the opponents of the Prophet of the judgment that will overtake them (vv. 1–8), the sūrah cites the people of Noah

STUDYQURAN:54:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r1.claim: The Hour refers to the Final Hour and the world’s imminent demise.
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r1.anchor: The Hour refers to the Final Hour as well as the imminent demise of the world (IK)

STUDYQURAN:54:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r2.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r2.claim: The Hour also refers to the Resurrection, as in verses 21:1 and 16:1.
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r2.anchor: and to the Resurrection (JJ), as in 21:1: For mankind, their reckoning draws nigh, while they turn away heedless

STUDYQURAN:54:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r3.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r3.claim: Hadith describe little time remaining between the Prophet’s coming and the world’s end relative to Earth’s lifespan; he illustrated this by pointing to his index and middle fingers.
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r3.anchor: I was sent like this in relation to the Hour,” while pointing to his index finger and his middle finger

STUDYQURAN:54:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r4.speaker: a few commentators
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r4.claim: A few commentators read the moon’s cleaving as a future end-time sign, though those who report this reading also mention the Prophet’s moon-splitting miracle.
STUDYQURAN:54:1/r4.anchor: A few commentators note that the second half of this verse could be read, “and the moon will be cleaved,” referring to one of the signs of the end of time

TAB-FULL:v22p107/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p107/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v22p107/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that at Mina the moon split, one part going behind a mountain, and the Prophet told the people to bear witness.
TAB-FULL:v22p107/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمنى، فانشق القمر، فأخذت فرقة خلف الجبل

TAB-FULL:v22p107/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p107/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v22p107/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says he saw the mountain through the opening between the two parts of the moon.
TAB-FULL:v22p107/r2.anchor: عن الأسود، عن عبد الله قال: «رأيت الجبل من فرج القمر حين انشق»

TAB-FULL:v22p107/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p107/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v22p107/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Quraysh called the split magic, asked travelers who confirmed seeing it, and then the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v22p107/r3.anchor: عن مسروق، عن عبد الله قال

TAB-FULL:v22p110/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r1.speaker: حذيفة
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r1.claim: In his sermon, Hudhayfa says the Hour is near and the moon has split; today is the racecourse, tomorrow the contest, with Paradise the prize and the Fire the destination.
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r1.anchor: وكان عطاء يروي أنه حذيفة فقال في هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v22p110/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r2.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r2.claim: Jubayr ibn Mutim reports that the moon split while he and others were with the Messenger in Mecca.
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن جبير بن مطعم، عن أبيه قال: «انشق القمر

TAB-FULL:v22p110/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the moon split in the time of the Messenger, before the Hijra, and that people saw its two halves.
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r3.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس قال: «انشق القمر قبل الهجرة»

TAB-FULL:v22p110/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the split happened at Mecca during the Prophet's time; the polytheists turned away and called it persistent magic.
TAB-FULL:v22p110/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه قال في هذه الآية: {اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر}

TAB-FULL:v22p111/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r1.claim: Mujahid says the people saw the moon split; in fuller reports, one half remained while the other went behind a mountain, and the Prophet called witnesses, including Abu Bakr.

TAB-FULL:v22p111/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r2.speaker: رجل
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r2.claim: An unnamed man preaching in Mada'in recites the verse and urges listeners to prepare for the race of deeds: Paradise is the goal and the Fire the end.

TAB-FULL:v22p111/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r3.claim: Qatada invokes the verse to affirm that God brings about whatever He wills in His creation.

TAB-FULL:v22p111/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r4.claim: Anas reports that Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign and the moon split twice in Mecca.
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r4.anchor: عن أنس قال: «سأل أهل مكة النبي

TAB-FULL:v22p111/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says the split had already occurred in Mecca during the Prophet's time; the polytheists turned away and called it magic.
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r5.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {وانشق القمر} [القمر: 1]

TAB-FULL:v22p111/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r6.claim: Ibrahim says the moon's splitting at Mecca has already passed.
TAB-FULL:v22p111/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: «مضى انشقاق القمر بمكة»

BURSEVI:v9p214/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214/r1.claim: The sūra has fifty-five verses and, according to the majority, is Meccan.
BURSEVI:v9p214/r1.anchor: وآياتها خمس وخمسون وهي مكية عند الجمهور

BURSEVI:v9p214/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214/r3.claim: The Hour, a portion of time, names the Resurrection by analogy: its reckoning is swift, it may come at the world's final hour, or be a brief interval containing a great event.
BURSEVI:v9p214/r3.anchor: والساعة جزء من أجزاء الزمان عبر بها عن القيامة تشبيها لها بذلك لسرعة حسابها

BURSEVI:v9p214/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214/r4.claim: The Resurrection is near because little of the world remains; the Prophet compares the world's remainder to a little of a little and a pool after its clear water has gone.
BURSEVI:v9p214/r4.anchor: والمعنى دنت القيامة وقرب قيامها ووقوعها لأنه ما بقي من الدنيا إلا قليل

BURSEVI:v9p214/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p214/r5.claim: The Prophet says God made the whole world little, so what remains is a little of a little, like a pool whose clear water is gone and only murk remains.
BURSEVI:v9p214/r5.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : إن الله جعل الدنيا كلها قليلا فما بقي منها قليل من قليل

BURSEVI:v9p214/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214/r6.claim: Bursevī associates the Hour with a seven-thousand-year cycle ending at Jesus' appearance: the Prophet's community exceeds a thousand years by roughly four to five hundred, and Adam and Jesus mark its opening and close.
BURSEVI:v9p214/r6.anchor: وقد صح أن مدة هذه الأمة تزيد على ألف بنحو أربعمائة سنة إلى خمسمائة سنة

BURSEVI:v9p214/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p214/r7.claim: He cites a report that portents occur after two hundred years and the Mahdi after two hundred, using it in his proposed chronology.
BURSEVI:v9p214/r7.anchor: وقد قال عليه السلام : الآيات بعد المائتين والمهدي بعد المائتين

BURSEVI:v9p214/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214/r8.claim: Scholars agree the world is created but have not fixed its duration; Bursevī proposes 360,000 years by scaling a Virgo cycle to an afterlife week of seven thousand years.
BURSEVI:v9p214/r8.anchor: اتفقوا على حدوث الدنيا وما قطعوا بشيء في مدتها والذي يلوح لي والله أعلم بحقيقة المدة أنها ثلاثمائة وستون ألف سنة

BURSEVI:v9p214/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v9p214/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited as saying the world is one week of the afterlife, or seven thousand years; Bursevī says 6,100 have passed and quotes the earth telling Adam its youth had ended.
BURSEVI:v9p214/r9.anchor: وعليه يحمل ما ورد عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما الدنيا جمعة من جمع الآخرة سبعة آلاف سنة

BURSEVI:v9p214/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214/r10.claim: He says the remaining world will include a time with no one worshipping God and transmits the saying that Adam arrived after the world's youth had passed, estimating roughly sixty thousand years gone.
BURSEVI:v9p214/r10.anchor: فقد مضى ستة آلاف سنة ومائة سنة وليأتين عليها زمن من سنين ليس عليها من يوحد

BURSEVI:v9p214/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214/r11.claim: Adam and the Prophet's existence are portents of the Hour; consequently the Prophet's miracles, including the moon's split, are signs of its approach.
BURSEVI:v9p214/r11.anchor: فآدم ونبينا عليهما السلام أي وجودهما من أشراط الساعة كما قال عليه السلام : مثلي ومثل الساعة كفرسي رهان

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r1.claim: Bursevī also relays a view that the world lasts seventy thousand years as part of the proposed calculation of its age.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r1.anchor: سبعون ألف سنة فاعرف جدا فالساعة مقتربة عند الله وعند الناس

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r2.claim: The Hour is near to God and people because every coming event is near, however long it takes; its nearness to God contrasts with heedless deniers' view that it is far away.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r2.anchor: فالساعة مقتربة عند الله وعند الناس لأن كل آت قريب وإن طالت مدته

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r3.claim: Announcing the Hour's approach warns morally responsible people and urges obedience by alerting creation to a great cosmic event.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r3.anchor: والحكمة في ذكر اقتراب الساعة تحذير المكلف وحثه على الطاعة تنبيها لعباده

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r4.claim: God alone knows the Hour's timing and conceals it because that is better for people; every prophet warned his community about the Dajjāl.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r4.anchor: وأما تعيين وقت الساعة فقد انفرد الحق تعالى بعلمه وأخفاه عن عباده لأنه أصلح لهم

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r5.claim: A hadith warns that liars will appear before the Hour; Bursevī identifies them as Dajjāls and misleading leaders.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن بين يدي الساعة كذابين فاحذروهم" والمراد بالكذابين الدجاجلة وهم الأئمة المضلون

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r6.claim: Prophets warned against impostors within their own communities, since no era lacked them; the one-eyed Dajjāl would come later, in the second millennium after two hundred.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r6.anchor: لا شك أن إنذار الأنبياء عليهم السلام حقيقة من أمثال هؤلاء الدجاجلة من أممهم إذ لم يخل قرن منهم

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r7.claim: Every earlier impostor, before or after the Prophet's mission, anticipates the known Dajjāl, just as every truthful person anticipates the Mahdi.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r7.anchor: فكل كذاب بين يدي الساعة سواء كان قبل مبعث النبي عليه السلام أو بعده فإنما هو من مقدمات الدجال المعروف

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r8.claim: The past tense indicates the moon actually split during the Prophet's lifetime; Ḥudhayfa's reading adds 'already,' marking a sign that the Hour drew near.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r8.anchor: دلت صيغة الماضي على تحقق الانشقاق في زمن النبي عليه السلام ويدل عليه قراءة حذيفة رضي الله عنه وقد انشق القمر

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r9.speaker: حذيفة
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r9.claim: Ḥudhayfa preached at al-Madāʾin that the Hour had drawn near and the moon had split in the Prophet's era.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r9.anchor: وقد خطب حذيفة بالمدائن ثم قال إلا أن الساعة قد اقتربت وأن القمر قد انشق على عهد نبيكم

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r10.claim: The majority of Companions and exegetes held that the split already occurred; Bursevī rejects the claim that it will happen only at the Resurrection, as with the sky's split.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا القول عامة الصحابة ومن بعدهم وبه أخذ أكثر المفسرين فلا عبرة بقول من قال إنه سينشق يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r11.claim: The moon may have split twice: in the Prophet's time as a sign of the approaching Hour, and again at the Resurrection when the sky splits.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r11.anchor: على أنا نقول يجوز أن يكون انشقاقه مرتين : مرة في زمانه عليه السلام إشارة إلى قرب الساعة

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r12.speaker: ابن حجر
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r12.claim: Ibn Ḥajar says reports of the tree trunk's moaning and moon's split are so widespread that they give certainty to those examining their transmission routes.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r12.anchor: وفي فتح الباري لابن حجر حنين الجذع وانشقاق القمر نقل كل منهما نقلا مستفيضا يفيد القطع

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r13.speaker: الطيبي
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r13.claim: Al-Ṭībī says Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj included nineteen reports, save one, tracing the moon's split to the Prophet in his commentary.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r13.anchor: وقال الطيبي : انسد أبو إسحاق الزجاج عشرين حديثا إلا واحدا في تفسيره إلى رسول الله عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r14.speaker: شرح الشريف للمواقف
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r14.claim: The commentary on al-Mawāqif calls the split mass-transmitted and says many Companions, including Ibn Masʿūd, reported it.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r14.anchor: وفي شرح الشريف للمواقف هذا متواتر رواه جمع كثير من الصحابة كابن مسعود وغيره

BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r15.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r15.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī questions classing this report as mass-transmitted: even the hadith about fabricating against the Prophet, narrated by sixty or more Companions including the Ten, was not so classed.
BURSEVI:v9p214#2/r15.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي فيه إنهم لم يجعلوا حديث من كذب علي متعمدا فليتبوأ مقعده من النار

TABATABAI:54:1-2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r1.claim: The Meccan sūra is chiefly a warning, opens with the moon-splitting sign and the deniers’ rejection, recalls judgment and ruined peoples, then closes with glad tidings for the pious.
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r1.anchor: سورة ممحضة في الإنذار والتخويف إلا آيتين من آخرها تبشران المتقين بالجنة والحضور عند ربهم

TABATABAI:54:1-2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r2.claim: The sūra is Meccan by its context; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī dismisses claims that it was revealed at Badr or that some verses are Medinan.

TABATABAI:54:1-2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r3.claim: Iqtirāb means an increase in nearness, so the Hour has drawn very near; al-sāʿa is the time when Resurrection occurs.

TABATABAI:54:1-2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r4.claim: The moon split means it separated into two parts, becoming two segments.
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r4.anchor: انفصل بعضه عن بعض فصار فرقتين شقتين

TABATABAI:54:1-2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r5.claim: The verse points to God’s sign of splitting the moon through the Prophet in Mecca before the Hijra, after Meccan polytheists requested it.
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r5.anchor: تشير الآية إلى آية شق القمر

TABATABAI:54:1-2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r6.claim: Reports about the split are abundant, and hadith scholars and exegetes are said to have accepted them.

TABATABAI:54:1-2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r7.speaker: الحسن وعطاء والبلخي
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan, ʿAṭāʾ, and al-Balkhī take the verse to predict a future split at the Hour, with past tense expressing certainty of occurrence.
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r7.anchor: إلا الحسن وعطاء والبلخي حيث قالوا

TABATABAI:54:1-2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r8.claim: He rejects the future-split reading: the next verse says they saw a sign, turned away, and called it persistent magic, which fits an event already shown to them.
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r8.anchor: فإن سياقها أوضح شاهد على أن قوله

TABATABAI:54:1-2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r9.claim: He rejects identifying the verse with the modern theory that the moon separated from Earth: 54:2 describes people calling a manifest sign magic, and no one called that scientific fact magic.
TABATABAI:54:1-2/r9.anchor: ما قيل إن الآية إشارة إلى ما ذهب إليه الرياضيون أخيرا أن القمر قطعة من الأرض

TABATABAI:54:1-8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r1.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r1.claim: Jubayr reports that the moon split at Mecca in the Prophet’s time into two parts, each appearing over a mountain; people accused Muhammad of magic, but one man said he could not bewitch everyone.
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r1.anchor: عن جبير بن مطعم في قوله { وانشق القمر } قال انشق القمر ونحن بمكة

TABATABAI:54:1-8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the event had already occurred before the Hijra and people saw the two halves.
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر } قال قد مضى ذلك قبل الهجرة

TABATABAI:54:1-8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r3.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r3.claim: In a sermon transmitted by Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, Ḥudhayfa says the moon split in the Prophet’s time, the Hour is near, and worldly life is nearing its end; today is preparation and tomorrow the race.
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r3.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال خطبنا حذيفة بن اليمان بالمدائن

TABATABAI:54:1-8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r4.claim: The split is reported through numerous routes from Anas, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar, Jubayr, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ḥudhayfa; al-Ālūsī also lists ʿAlī among the Companions who transmitted it.
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r4.anchor: وقد روي انشقاق القمر بدعاء النبي

TABATABAI:54:1-8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r5.speaker: السيد الشريف وابن السبكي
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r5.claim: Al-Sayyid al-Sharīf and Ibn al-Subkī call the report mutawātir and say its mass transmission is beyond doubt.
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r5.anchor: عن السيد الشريف في شرح المواقف وعن ابن السبكي في شرح المختصر أن الحديث متواتر

TABATABAI:54:1-8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes the report’s standing among Sunni scholars and says its standing among Shiʿites was established earlier in the discussion.
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r6.anchor: هذه حال الحديث عند أهل السنة وقد عرفت حاله عند الشيعة

TABATABAI:54:1-8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r7.claim: Muslims accept the moon-splitting sign in Mecca before the Hijra at the polytheists’ request; Qur’an 54:2 and numerous reports from both groups support an actual event near revelation.
TABATABAI:54:1-8/r7.anchor: آية شق القمر بيد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بمكة

TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r1.claim: Qur’an 54:2 requires that the moon split be a sign occurring near the time of revelation, which the polytheists rejected like other signs; proliferating reports from both Muslim groups also support it.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r1.anchor: فالآية الثانية تأبى إلا أن يكون مدلول قوله

TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r2.claim: The Qur’an and Sunna establish the sign; splitting a celestial body is rationally possible, miracles can occur, and the event should be accepted though it is not among religion’s necessities.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r2.anchor: فالكتاب والسنة يدلان عليها وانشقاق كرة من الكرات الجوية

TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r3.claim: The objection reads Qur’an 17:59 as withholding signs because earlier peoples denied them, either predicting this community’s denial too or avoiding the annihilation that followed earlier rejection.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r3.anchor: مفاد الآية إما أنا لا نرسل بالآيات

TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r4.claim: Qur’an 17:59 concerns signs requested by people, not signs that support a messenger or wonders God grants graciously; the requested-sign policy addresses their expected denial and ensuing punishment.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#2/r4.anchor: نعم هذا في الآيات المرسلة باقتراح من الناس دون الآيات التي تؤيد بها الرسالة

TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r1.claim: The requested-sign objection is reinforced by Qur’an 17:90–93, where the people demand a spring from the earth and the Prophet is told to say he is only a human messenger.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r1.anchor: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r2.claim: The Prophet was sent to all humanity as the final prophet, as shown by Qur’an 7:158, 6:19, and 33:40.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r2.anchor: قل يا أيها الناس إني رسول الله إليكم جميعا

TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r3.claim: At Mecca the Prophet faced hostility, abuse, mockery, and plots to expel or kill him, until God ordered the Hijra; many nevertheless believed while the larger public remained hostile.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r3.anchor: فقابلوه بما استطاعوا من الشقاق والإيذاء والاستهزاء وهموا بإخراجه أو إثباته أو قتله حتى أمره ربه بالهجرة

TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r4.claim: Qur’an 4:77, in a reported occasion of revelation, shows believers had asked permission to fight and were told to restrain themselves, indicating a community of some size despite persecution.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r4.anchor: كما يدل عليه قوله تعالى ألم تر إلى الذين قيل لهم كفوا أيديكم وأقيموا الصلاة

TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r5.claim: After the Hijra Islam spread through Medina, nearby regions, tribes, Yemen, and Arabia outside Mecca; in year six the Prophet wrote to rulers of Persia, Rome, and Egypt, and Mecca was conquered in year eight.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r5.anchor: ثم بسط الدعوة على غير الجزيرة فكاتب الملوك والعظماء من فارس والروم ومصر سنة ست من الهجرة

TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r6.claim: Many Meccans converted between the Hijra and conquest, most converted at the conquest, and Islam continued to grow until its adherents numbered about one fifth of the earth’s population.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r6.anchor: وقد أسلم ما بين الهجرة والفتح جمع من أهلها وحواليها

TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r7.claim: The requested split would entail punishment if denied, but the Prophet’s universal mission meant all humanity could not then be destroyed before the proof was complete; the event occurred five years before the Hijra.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#3/r7.anchor: كانت آية انشقاق القمر آية اقتراحية تستعقب

TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r1.claim: Qur’an 8:42 requires that destruction follow clear proof; Qur’an 48:25 says believers were among Mecca’s people, so God would not annihilate the city while they remained there.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r1.anchor: ما كان الله ليهلك جميع أهل مكة وحواليها

TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r2.claim: God would not spare believers while annihilating disbelievers when many Meccans later accepted Islam, for Islam accepted outward profession; the obstinate leaders and mockers were the deniers described in Qur’an 2:6, and they were destroyed at Badr.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r2.anchor: وما كان الله سبحانه لينجي المؤمنين ويهلك كفارهم وقد آمن جمع كثير منهم فيما بين سنة خمس قبل الهجرة وسنة ثمان بعد الهجرة

TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r3.claim: Qur’an 17:59 cannot include signs supporting the mission or gracious wonders; if general, it restricts only requested signs, withheld because Quraysh would deny them and God did not wish to punish them immediately.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#4/r3.anchor: فالآية لا تشمل قطعا الآيات المؤيدة للرسالة

TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r1.claim: Qur’an 8:33 says the Prophet’s presence and people’s seeking forgiveness prevented punishment; Qur’an 17:76 warns that expelling him would have brought their destruction soon afterward.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r1.anchor: وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم وما كان الله معذبهم وهم يستغفرون

TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r2.claim: Qur’an 8:34–35, revealed after Badr, shows there was no remaining barrier to punishment once the Prophet was gone; the Meccans then suffered the slaughter at Badr.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r2.anchor: والآيات تبين أنه لم يكن من قبلهم مانع من نزول العذاب

TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r3.claim: Denial by earlier peoples and the Prophet’s presence restrained signs and immediate punishment; after grounds such as obstructing worship and mocking arose and he left, a sign could establish the case and punishment follow rejection.

TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r4.claim: Qur’an 17:59 withholds signs while the Prophet is among the people; it does not rule out sending a sign and delaying punishment until after his departure. Badr itself was a sign and punishment.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r4.anchor: إنما يفيد الإمساك عن إرسال الآيات

TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r5.claim: Even if signs were withheld as useless before people predisposed to deny them, the moon split could prove the truth and falsehood could be undone, with punishment deferred until the Prophet left.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r5.anchor: فإن إرسالها مع تأخير العذاب والنكال

TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r6.claim: Qur’an 17:93 does not deny prophetic miracles: that would contradict the Qur’an’s accounts of earlier miracles and the miraculous Qur’an itself; the Prophet means he cannot produce signs by himself, since their power belongs to God.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#5/r6.anchor: فليس مدلوله نفي تأييد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r1.claim: The Prophet says signs belong to God and come only by His will; Noah’s reply and Qur’an 13:38 likewise say a messenger brings a sign only by God’s permission.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r1.anchor: قل إنما الآيات عند الله وما يشعركم

TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r2.claim: An objection argues that a lunar split would have been seen everywhere and recorded by eastern and western astronomers, given its exceptional nature and the many incentives to transmit it.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r2.anchor: ومن الاعتراض على آية الانشقاق ما قيل إن القمر لو انشق كما يقال لرآه جميع الناس ولضبطه أهل الأرصاد في الشرق والغرب

TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r3.claim: People may simply have missed the event; not every earthly or celestial occurrence is known, preserved, and inherited from one generation to the next.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r3.anchor: أن من الممكن أولا أن يغفل عنه فلا دليل على كون كل حادث أرضي أو سماوي معلوما للناس محفوظا عندهم

TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r4.claim: Arabia had no observatory for celestial phenomena; observatories existed in India and western lands, but none is established for this time, reported as the first night of 14 Dhū al-Ḥijja, five years before the Hijra.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r4.anchor: أن الحجاز وما حولها من البلاد العربية

TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r5.claim: The moon was reportedly full, split briefly near sunset as it rose at Mecca, then rejoined; by the time it rose over western lands, it appeared whole.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r5.anchor: وقد كان القمر - على ما في بعض الروايات - بدرا

TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r6.claim: He suspects non-Muslim church and polytheist adherents of withholding reports on religious matters that would benefit Islam.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r6.anchor: على أنا نتهم غير المسلمين من أتباع الكنيسة والوثنية في الأمور الدينية التي لها مساس نفع بالإسلام

TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r7.claim: The claim that gravity must fail for the halves to separate and thus they could never rejoin is unproved as a rational impossibility; if custom forbade rejoining, it should equally forbid splitting, and miracles break customary patterns.
TABATABAI:54:1-8#6/r7.anchor: والجواب عنه أن الاستحالة العقلية ممنوعة

TABRISI:54:1-10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:1-10/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:54:1-10/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the moon split into two parts during the Prophet's time, and the Prophet told those present to bear witness.
TABRISI:54:1-10/r1.anchor: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شقتين

TABRISI:54:1-10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:1-10/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:54:1-10/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd also swears that he saw Mount Ḥirāʾ between the two halves of the moon.
TABRISI:54:1-10/r2.anchor: وروي أيضا عن ابن مسعود أنه قال والذي نفسي بيده لقد رأيت حراء

TABRISI:54:1-10/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:1-10/r3.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
TABRISI:54:1-10/r3.claim: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim says the moon split into two parts above two mountains; when some said Muḥammad had bewitched them, another replied that he could not have bewitched everyone.
TABRISI:54:1-10/r3.anchor: وعن جبير بن مطعم قال: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله

TABRISI:54:1-10/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:1-10/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:54:1-10/r4.claim: Many Companions transmitted the splitting, and the commentators affirm it; the author rejects the future-tense interpretation attributed to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ from his father and to al-Hasan, also rejected by al-Balkhī.
TABRISI:54:1-10/r4.anchor: وقد روى حديث انشقاق القمر جماعة كثيرة من الصحابة

TABRISI:54:1-10/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:1-10/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:54:1-10/r5.claim: The author says the objection that such an event could not have gone unnoticed fails: clouds could conceal it, it happened at night when people might sleep, and not everyone watches the sky.
TABRISI:54:1-10/r5.anchor: لأنه يجوز أن يكون الله تعالى قد حجبه عن أكثرهم بغيم

TABRISI:54:1-10/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:1-10/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:54:1-10/r6.claim: The moon's splitting is a sign of the Prophet's mission, and his mission and era are among the signs that the Hour is approaching.
TABRISI:54:1-10/r6.anchor: لأن انشقاقه من علامة نبوة نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:54:1-10#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:54:1-10#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:54:1-10#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes the wording as evidence that the splitting occurred; a miracle is needed to prove prophethood while people can choose, not when they are compelled to know.
TABRISI:54:1-10#2/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج وفي هذا دلالة على أن ذلك قد كان ووقع

THALABI:v9p160#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p160#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p160#3/r1.claim: The Hour has drawn near: the Resurrection is approaching.

THALABI:v9p160#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p160#3/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v9p160#3/r2.claim: Ibn Kaysān sees inversion of sequence: the sense is that the moon split and then the Hour approached, supported by a reading attributed to Ḥudhayfa, وقد انشق القمر.
THALABI:v9p160#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن كيسان: في الآية تقديم وتأخير، مجازها: انشق القمر واقتربت الساعة، يدل عليه قراءة حذيفة

THALABI:v9p160#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p160#3/r3.speaker: عثمان بن عطاء
THALABI:v9p160#3/r3.claim: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ, transmitting from his father, says the phrase means the moon will split in the future; the commentators disagree and sound reports say the event already occurred.
THALABI:v9p160#3/r3.anchor: وروى عثمان بن عطاء عن أبيه أن معناه: (وسينشق القمر)

THALABI:v9p160#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p160#3/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p160#3/r4.claim: The author rejects the future reading: scholars oppose it, and sound reports establish that the sign has already occurred.
THALABI:v9p160#3/r4.anchor: والعلماء على خلافه والأخبار الصحاح ناطقة بأن هذه الآية قد مضت

THALABI:v9p160#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p160#3/r5.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v9p160#3/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reports that in the Prophet's time the moon split into two halves, one above and one below a mountain, and the Prophet called God to witness and told people to bear witness.
THALABI:v9p160#3/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله أن القمر انشق على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرقتين، فكانت إحداهما فوق الجبل

THALABI:v9p160#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p160#3/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v9p160#3/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the moon split in the Prophet's time and he saw its two halves.
THALABI:v9p160#3/r6.anchor: عن علقمة عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى رأيت فلقتيه

THALABI:v9p160#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p160#3/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v9p160#3/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar transmitted a report like Ibn Masʿūd's account of the moon splitting in the Prophet's time.
THALABI:v9p160#3/r7.anchor: عن سليمان عن مجاهد عن ابن عمر نحو حديث ابن مسعود

THALABI:v9p160#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p160#3/r8.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
THALABI:v9p160#3/r8.claim: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim reports from his father that the moon split while they were with the Prophet in Mecca.
THALABI:v9p160#3/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن جبير بن مطعم عن أبيه، قال: انشق القمر ونحن مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة

THALABI:v9p161/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p161/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p161/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the moon split in the Prophet's time into two parts, one over al-Suwaydāʾ and the other over al-Jandama.
THALABI:v9p161/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومقسم عن ابن عباس قال: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم باثنين: شطره على السويداء

THALABI:v9p161/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p161/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v9p161/r2.claim: Anas reports that Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign, and he showed them the moon split in two with the mountain visible between its parts.
THALABI:v9p161/r2.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك أن أهل مكة سألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يريهم آية، فأراهم القمر شقتين

THALABI:v9p161/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p161/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v9p161/r3.claim: Another report from Anas says the moon split twice in the Prophet's time.
THALABI:v9p161/r3.anchor: عن قتادة عن أنس قال: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مرتين

THALABI:v9p161/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p161/r4.speaker: حذيفة
THALABI:v9p161/r4.claim: In two Friday sermons, Ḥudhayfa says the Hour has drawn near, the moon has split, and the world is nearing its departure; today is the arena and tomorrow the race of deeds, whose finish is the Fire and whose winner reaches Paradise.
THALABI:v9p161/r4.anchor: فحضر أبي فحضرنا معه فخطبنا حذيفة، فقال: ألا إن الله سبحانه يقول: اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر، ألا فإن الساعة قد اقتربت

THALABI:v9p161/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p161/r5.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v9p161/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reports that after the moon split, Quraysh called it the magic of Ibn Abī Kabsha and asked travelers, who confirmed they had seen it; the verse was then revealed.
THALABI:v9p161/r5.anchor: عن مسروق عن عبد الله قال: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وقالت قريش: هذا سحر ابن أبي كبشة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p89#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p89#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p89#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that polytheists asked the Messenger to split the moon in two as proof; he asked whether they would believe if he did, and they agreed. It was a Badr night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p89#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: اجتمع المشركون إلى رسول الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:1-5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:1-5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:1-5/r1.claim: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon split as one of its signs of approach.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:1-5/r1.anchor: { اقتربت الساعة } دنت القيامة { وانشق القمر } انفلق بنصفين على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:1-5/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:1-5/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:1-5/r2.claim: At the Prophet’s time, Meccans requested a sign; he showed the moon split in two with Mount Hira visible between its halves.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:54:1-5/r2.anchor: فأراهم القمر فلقتين حتى رأوا حراء بينهما، فأخبر الله تعالى أن ذلك من علامات قرب الساعة.

QASHANI:54:1/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:54:1/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:54:1/r1.claim: For the great resurrection, the Moon is the two-sided heart, dark toward the soul and lit toward the spirit; its splitting by the spirit's light and the sun emerging from the heart's veil signal approaching annihilation in unity and essential witnessing.
QASHANI:54:1/r1.anchor: لأن القمر إشارة إلى القلب لكونه ذا وجهين

QASHANI:54:1/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:54:1/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:54:1/r2.claim: If read as the cycle of manifestation in the Mahdi's era, the Moon's splitting is its opening through Muhammad's appearance in the lunar cycle.
QASHANI:54:1/r2.anchor: وإن حملت على دور الظهور الذي هو زمان المهدي المبعوث في نسمها

QASHANI:54:1/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:54:1/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:54:1/r3.claim: For the minor resurrection, the Moon is the body, dark in itself and receiving sensation and life from the spirit as the Moon receives light from the Sun.
QASHANI:54:1/r3.anchor: فالقمر هو البدن لاستفادته نور الشعور والحياة من شمس الروح

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r1.claim: The Hour, when believers receive reward and disbelievers punishment, draws nearer day by day; people must prepare.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r1.anchor: Sâ‘at yaklaştı mü’minlere sevâbın, kâfirlere ikābın mev‘ud olduğu kıyamet vakti günden güne yaklaşmaktadır

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r2.speaker: Ashâb, tâbi‘în ve müteahhirîn müfessirlerinin umûmu
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r2.claim: Elmalılı says exegetes across generations agree that the verse reports the splitting-of-the-Moon miracle; the report is famous and transmitted by many Companions.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r2.anchor: mâlum olan müfessirlerin umûmu bunun şakk-ı Kamer

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas had not yet been born and Anas was four or five in Medina, but they transmitted the event; Ibn Masud and Jubayr b. Mut‘im witnessed it.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r3.anchor: İbn Abbas henüz doğmamıştı, Enes de Medine’de dört beş yaşlarında bulunuyordu

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r4.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r4.claim: Bukhari’s Ibn Masud report has the Moon split into two parts, one above and one below a mountain; the Prophet told them to witness it.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r4.anchor: Buhârî’de İbn Mes‘ûd’dan 1. “Resûlullah’ın devrinde Kamer iki fırkaya inşikak etti; bir fırka dağın fevkinde, bir fırka da dûnunda

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r5.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r5.claim: Bukhari’s report from Ibn Abbas says the Moon split during the Prophet’s time.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r5.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan: “Peygamber’in zamanında Kamer inşikak etti.”

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r6.speaker: Enes
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r6.claim: Bukhari reports that Meccans requested a sign and the Prophet showed them the Moon splitting into two parts.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r6.anchor: Enes’ten, “Mekke ahâlisi kendilerine bir âyet gösterilmesini istediler, Peygamber de Kamer’in inşikākını gösterdi”

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r7.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r7.claim: Muslim gives Ibn Masud’s report of two parts, with the mountain between them, and the Prophet’s command to witness.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r7.anchor: Müslim, İbn Mes‘ûd’dan: 1. “Resûlullah’ın ahdinde Kamer iki şıkka inşikak etti, Resûlullah ‘şâhid olun!’ buyurdu.”

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r8.speaker: Enes
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r8.claim: Muslim reports that Meccans requested a sign and the Prophet showed the Moon split, called merreteyn in one wording and firkateyn in another.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r8.anchor: Enes’ten: “Ehl-i Mekke Resûlullah’tan bir âyet göstermesini istediler, o da ‘merreteyn’ olarak Kamer’in inşikākını gösterdi”

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r9.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r9.claim: Muslim’s report from Ibn Abbas is noted as matching Bukhari’s account.

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r10.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r10.claim: At Mina, Ibn Masud says the Moon split, with one part beyond and one this side of the mountain; the Prophet said to witness and cited this verse.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r10.anchor: Tirmizî, İbn Mes‘ûd’dan: “Biz Resûlullah ile beraber Minâ’da idik Kamer iki filkaya inşikak etti, bir filka dağın ötesinde bir filka da berisinde

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r11.speaker: Enes
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r11.claim: Tirmidhi’s Anas report says Meccans requested a sign, the Moon split twice in Mecca, and the verses were then revealed.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r11.anchor: Enes’ten: “Ehl-i Mekke Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den bir âyet istediler, binâen‘aleyh Mekke’de

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r12.speaker: İbn Ömer
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r12.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Moon split during the Prophet’s time and he said, Witness.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r12.anchor: İbn Ömer’den: “Resûlullah’ın ahdinde Kamer yarıldı, Resûlullah ‘şâhid olun!’ buyurdu.”

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r13.speaker: Cübeyr b. Mut‘im
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r13.claim: Jubayr says the Moon split over two sides of a mountain; some called it magic, while others said magic could not affect everyone.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r13.anchor: Cübeyr b. Mut‘im’den: “Peygamber’in ahdinde Kamer inşikak etti, hatta iki fırka oldu

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r14.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r14.claim: The Shifa report transmitted by Abu Hudhayfa al-Arhabi from Ali says the Moon split while they were with the Messenger.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r14.anchor: Ebû Huzeyfe el-Erhabî rivayetiyle Hazret-i Ali’den: “Kamer inşikak etti, biz Resûlullah ile beraber idik.”

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r15.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r15.claim: In reports through Aswad, Ibn Masud says he saw the mountain between the Moon’s two clefts.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r15.anchor: Esved rivayetiyle İbn Mes‘ûd’dan: “Hatta cebeli, Kamer’in iki fürcesi arasında gördüm.”

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r16.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r16.claim: Through Masruq, Ibn Masud recounts Quraysh accusing Abu Kabsha’s son of magic; another says ask travelers from elsewhere, who confirmed seeing it.

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r17.speaker: Ebû Cehil (Semerkandî’nin nakline göre)
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r17.claim: Samarkandi says Abu Jahl called it magic and sent word abroad to ask whether others saw it; they confirmed, but Quraysh still called it lasting magic.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r17.anchor: Semerkandî’nin nakline göre Ebû Cehil “bu bir sihirdir, ehl-i âfâka haber salın gören olmuş mu bakalım” dedi

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r18.speaker: Huzeyfe
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r18.claim: In a sermon at Mada’in, Hudhayfa says the Hour truly approaches and the Moon truly split during the Prophet’s time; the world announces farewell.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r18.anchor: “Uyanın, Allah teâlâ ٱقْتَرَبَتِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ buyuruyor. Evet Sâ‘at cidden yaklaştı

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r19.claim: Elmalılı says these many narrations interpret the verse and, especially in Ibn Masud’s and Ibn Abbas’s wording, establish a past event; Ibn Masud elsewhere lists the Moon among five signs.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r19.anchor: Hâsılı bu bâbda hadis hayli çoktur, bütün bunlar âyetin tefsiri hakkında vârid olmuş rivayetlerdir.

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r20.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r20.claim: Alusi cites reports from several collections that Ibn Masud saw the Moon split into two clefts twice in Mecca before the Prophet’s mission.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r20.anchor: Âlûsî’nin nakline göre Abd b. Humeyd, Hâkim ve İbn Merdûye ve Beyhakī İbn Mes‘ûd’dan dahi

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r21.speaker: Irâkī
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r21.claim: Iraqi says the occurrence twice is agreed upon and writes that it split twice by consensus.

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r22.speaker: İbn Hacer
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r22.claim: Ibn Hajar knows no hadith scholar who asserts repeated occurrences; he says consensus concerns the split, and merreteyn likely means two pieces.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r22.anchor: Hâfız İbn Hacer de bunun hakkında demiştir ki: “Peygamber’in zamanında inşikākın ta‘addüdüne cezmeden ulemâ-yı hadisten kimse bilmiyorum

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r23.speaker: İbn İmâm-ı Cevziyye
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r23.claim: Ibn Imam Jawziyya explains that marraat can refer to things as well as acts; here it means two pieces, not separate occasions.

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r24.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r24.claim: Alusi argues that merreteyn qualifies seeing in Ibn Masud’s report: he saw the split twice, rather than the Moon splitting twice.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r24.anchor: Âlûsî İbn Mes‘ûd rivayetinde şıkkateyn merreteyn denilmiş olması hasebiyle bunun firkateyn mânasına olması yaraşmayacağını

ELMALILI:54:1-8/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r25.claim: Elmalılı concludes there was one event; during it the Moon separated and closed twice as rapidly as lightning, with a mountain visible between.
ELMALILI:54:1-8/r25.anchor: İnşikāk-ı Kamer vak‘ası iki değil birdir.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r1.speaker: Osman b. Atâ, babasından
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r1.claim: Abu Saud cites Uthman b. Ata from his father as saying the Moon will split on Judgment Day; some tafsirs attribute this view to Hasan al-Basri.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r1.anchor: Ebussuud’un nakline göre Osman b. Atâ babasından, سَيـَنْشَ ُّق

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r2.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r2.claim: Commentaries such as Nasafi also attribute the future-only reading to Hasan al-Basri.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r2.anchor: Nesefî gibi bazı tefsirlerde bu, Hasan-ı Basrî’ye de atfolunmuştur

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r3.claim: Although Quranic past tense can sometimes denote a certain future, Elmalılı rejects that reading here because the next verse describes people seeing a sign and turning away.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r3.anchor: Lâkin burada böyle bir te’vilin mânasız olacağı gösterilmiştir. Çünkü önündeki وَإِن يَرَوْا۟ âyeti bunu reddeyler.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r4.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r4.claim: Razi says all exegetes understand an actual past splitting and reports say the requested sign appeared after the Prophet prayed.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r4.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Müfessirînin hepsi murad

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r5.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r5.claim: Razi calls the future-only reading pointless: a philosopher who denies the miracle rejects it in either tense, while a believer need not reinterpret it.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r5.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Müfessirînin hepsi murad ‘Kamer münşak oldu, onda inşikak vukū‘a geldi’ demek olduğunu söylemişler

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r6.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r6.claim: Razi argues the split is possible and a sound report establishes it; the mutawatir Quran is the strongest proof, making further mass transmission unnecessary.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r6.anchor: Kamer’in yarılması haddizâtında mümkinâttandır, haber-i sâdık ile vukū‘u haber verilince inanmamaya sebep yoktur.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r7.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r7.claim: Razi says absent records by historians or astronomers do not justify denial, nor do claims that celestial bodies cannot rupture and rejoin.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r7.anchor: Hâriçteki müverrihlerin ve müneccimlerin farkına varamamasından veya bir husuf gibi telakkī etmesinden dolayı zabt u kayd etmemiş olmaları vak‘ayı inkâra hak veremeyeceği

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r8.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan says the community agrees against a future-only reading; verse 54:2 refutes it because that statement fits only after the requested sign appeared.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r8.anchor: Ebû Hayyân der ki: وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ kavlinin mânası kıyamette münşak olacaktır

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r9.speaker: Huzeyfe
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan cites Hudhayfa’s sermon affirming the Moon truly split in the Prophet’s time; Hasan’s claim of a split after the second trumpet is not to be followed.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r9.anchor: ‘âgâh olunuz ki Sâ‘at yaklaştı ve Peygamberimizin zamanında Kamer hakikaten münşak oldu’

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r10.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r10.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the claim that moon-splitting means moonrise, with darkness splitting as dawn does.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r10.anchor: “Kamer’in inşikākı, Ay doğduğu esnada zulmetin yarılmasından ibarettir

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r11.claim: Elmalılı calls the moonrise metaphor fallacious: although dawn is darkness parting, Moon-rise cannot be called Moon-splitting, and the Quran should be protected from this strained sense.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r12.claim: The miracle makes the Hour intellectually near by showing the Moon and other celestial bodies can split and collapse; nearness is not just chronological.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r12.anchor: inşikāk-ı Kamer mucizesi Sâ‘at’in zamanda yakınlığından ziyade akla yakınlığını göstermiştir

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r13.claim: Elmalılı says Hasan and Ata were misunderstood: they did not deny the past miracle but drew out its indication of a future cosmic split.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r13.anchor: Onlar, Kamer’in kıyamette inşikak edeceğini söylemekle, geçmiş olan inşikāk-ı Kamer vak‘asını inkâr edivermiş gibi farzedilmiştir.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r14.claim: The past split shows celestial bodies may split at the Hour, when Sun and Moon are joined.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r14.anchor: mâzî olan inşikākın müstakbeldeki inşikāka bir delâleti

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r15.claim: The past event also implies that the Hour and the Prophet’s victory over the polytheists are near.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r15.anchor: Kamer’in inşikākı bir emr-i vâki‘dir, mâzîde vâki‘olan bu inşikak

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r16.claim: Elmalılı places the philosophical debate in kalam; Razi observed that the philosopher denies both past and future splitting.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r16.anchor: Felsefe bakımından meselenin münakaşası ilm-i kelâm meselesidir.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r17.claim: For those unable to conceive miracles, Elmalılı says first direct attention to creation’s wonders, as the Quran often does, then introduces Ibn Sina’s words.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#2/r17.anchor: mu‘cizâtı tasavvur edemeyenlere karşı ilk yapılacak iş Kur’ân’ın birçok yerlerinde yapıldığı vechile hilkatteki acâibâta nazar-ı dikkati celbetmektir

ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r1.speaker: İbn Sînâ
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r1.claim: Ibn Sina urges withholding judgment on reports of an arif's prayers bringing rain or healing, averting disasters, or affecting animals, since hidden natural causes may underlie such wonders.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r2.speaker: İbn Sînâ
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r2.claim: Ibn Sina traces unseen natural effects to psychic constitution, properties of elemental bodies, or celestial forces, associating magic with the first, miracles and saintly wonders with the second, and talismans with the third.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r3.speaker: İbn Sînâ
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r3.claim: Ibn Sina says denial without proof is as irrational as credulous assent; when a report seems strange, suspend judgment unless there is proof it is impossible, because nature holds many marvels.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r4.claim: Elmalılı says Ibn Sina wrongly treated the heavens and celestial bodies as simple, non-elemental, untouchable substances whose lack of rectilinear-motion inclination made them incapable of being torn or corrupted.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r4.anchor: İbn Sînâ teessüf olunur ki ilm-i tabîî nâmına nazariyesinde yanlış bir fikre zâhib olmuş

ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r5.claim: Elmalılı argues that allowing a body's inclination to circular motion while excluding inclination to straight motion is an unsupported contradiction, since direction is accidental to motion and any obstacle needs a separate account.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r5.anchor: Birinin câiz olabildiği bir yerde diğeri de câiz olabilir.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r6.claim: Elmalılı says stars and their spheres are composed of elemental matter like Earth and can undergo generation and corruption, in accord with the scientific and philosophical views of his time.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r6.anchor: Onlar da Arz gibi ecsâm-ı unsuriyeden mürekkeb ve binâen‘aleyh kevn ü fesâdı kābildirler.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#3/r7.claim: Given theories that the Moon separated from Earth, a philosopher may read the verse as a past event, but cannot use that reading to deny either the prophetic miracle or a future splitting at the Resurrection.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r1.claim: Modern science does not deny that the Moon can split; Elmalılı lists internal explosion, external currents, waves, collision, elasticity, or pressure as conceivable mechanisms, while leaving the necessary force undetermined.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r1.anchor: Bugünkü fen Kamer’i bir cism-i esîrî farzetmediği gibi yarılabilmek kābiliyetini de inkâr etmez.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r2.claim: The actual agent is God's power and will; no messenger brings a sign except by God's leave.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r2.anchor: mevzû‘-i bahis olan müessir ise Allah teâlâ’nın kudret ve iradesidir.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r3.claim: Elmalılı contrasts the knowledge-and-witnessing nearness disclosed in the Najm account with the volitional nearness manifested in the Moon's splitting at the Messenger's request.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r3.anchor: Sûre-i Necm’de “şedîdü’l-kuvâ”nın tâlimiyle istivâdan sonra kābe kavseyni ev ednâ tedellîsinde rü’yet-i âyât ile tecellî eden kurb-i ilmî ve şuhûdî

ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r4.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r4.claim: Ibn Arabi describes the Moon as an intermediate station between crescent and full Moon: hilal names its appearance, badr its light filling the eye, and mihak its concealment by sunlight.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r4.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Fütûhât’ının üç yüz otuzuncu bâbında Hazret-i Muhammediyeden menzil-i Kamer’i marifet hakkında berzahî bir ifade ile şöyle der:

ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r5.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r5.claim: Ibn Arabi reads the Moon's changing stations as a sign for recognizing the Perfect Human and attaining knowledge of God; its waxing and waning exemplify transitions between the unseen and witnessed realms, and its splitting images manifestation in two forms.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r5.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Fütûhât’ının üç yüz otuzuncu bâbında Hazret-i Muhammediyeden menzil-i Kamer’i marifet hakkında berzahî bir ifade ile şöyle der:

ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r6.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r6.claim: Ibn Arabi cites a Companion report that the Moon split during the Prophet's time after Arabs asked for a sign, and the Prophet told those present to bear witness.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r6.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Fütûhât’ının üç yüz otuzuncu bâbında Hazret-i Muhammediyeden menzil-i Kamer’i marifet hakkında berzahî bir ifade ile şöyle der:

ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r7.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r7.claim: Ibn Arabi says it is uncertain whether the verse means the very splitting requested by the Arabs, though the following account of their seeing a sign and calling it magic makes that the apparent reading.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r7.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Fütûhât’ının üç yüz otuzuncu bâbında Hazret-i Muhammediyeden menzil-i Kamer’i marifet hakkında berzahî bir ifade ile şöyle der:

ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r10.speaker: Fennî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r10.claim: Fennî reads Ibn Arabi as allowing that the split occurred only in viewers' eyes, but argues it could still be a true miracle because no sorcerer is known to project an illusion onto a celestial body.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#4/r10.anchor: Maddiyyûn Mezhebinin İzmihlâli nâm kitabında Bay İsmail Fennî

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r1.claim: Elmalılı rejects the proposed defense of an eye-only splitting: presenting an unreal event as real is still deception and incompatible with prophetic sanctity, and that is precisely what the deniers meant by calling it magic.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r1.anchor: Böyle bir cevap hiç de doğru olmaz. İtiraf etmek lâzım gelir ki gerek kavilde olsun gerek fiilde

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r2.claim: Elmalılı says Ibn Arabi narrates the splitting as an actual event throughout; his disputed words describe the deniers' own uncertain, intermediate viewpoint, not Ibn Arabi's endorsement of an optical illusion, and 53:30 concerns those deniers.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r2.anchor: Şeyh’in anlattığı da budur. O, kelâmının bütün cereyânında inşikāk-ı Kamer’i bir vak‘a olarak anlatmıştır.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r3.speaker: Şeyh
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r3.claim: Ibn Arabi says reflection and observation lead from visible things to hidden truths, with witnessing higher than thought; he connects this movement to the signs for the pious and thinkers.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r3.anchor: Onun için Şeyh o sözler arkasından şu ihtârı yapar: “Yine bil ki nazar ve itibar, esrâr ve envârdan

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r4.speaker: Şeyh
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r4.claim: Ibn Arabi says God teaches the pious so doubt does not enter their knowledge, while thinkers depend on fallible created powers; the thinker lies between eyesight and pure insight.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r4.anchor: Onun için Şeyh o sözler arkasından şu ihtârı yapar: “Yine bil ki nazar ve itibar, esrâr ve envârdan

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r5.speaker: Fennî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r5.claim: Fennî says the majority rejects the report from Uthman b. Ata's father that the split belongs to the Resurrection, relying on Companion reports and the clear indication of 54:2, and accepts a Prophetic-era miracle.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r5.anchor: Mûmâ ileyh Fennî Bay da kelâmının sonunda hiss-i takvâsıyla basiretine sahip

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r6.speaker: Fennî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r6.claim: Fennî professes that God can do all things, natural laws are only consequences of His command Be, and the Qur'an is wholly true; he therefore accepts the Moon's real splitting without hesitation, leaving its manner to God and His Messenger.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r6.anchor: Mûmâ ileyh Fennî Bay da kelâmının sonunda hiss-i takvâsıyla basiretine sahip

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r7.speaker: Fennî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r7.claim: Fennî answers that people around the event and in other regions saw the Moon split; differing horizons, clouds, people indoors, and lack of sky-watching explain why it was not seen everywhere.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r7.anchor: Mûmâ ileyh Fennî Bay da kelâmının sonunda hiss-i takvâsıyla basiretine sahip

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r8.speaker: Fennî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r8.claim: Fennî says the event may have gone unrecorded in that age of ignorance because people attributed it to sorcerers, jinn, or devils.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r8.anchor: Mûmâ ileyh Fennî Bay da kelâmının sonunda hiss-i takvâsıyla basiretine sahip

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r9.speaker: Fennî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r9.claim: Fennî warns that reducing miracles to natural laws makes them ordinary; human reason cannot grasp the nature of supernatural events and errs when applied beyond its competence.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r9.anchor: Mûmâ ileyh Fennî Bay da kelâmının sonunda hiss-i takvâsıyla basiretine sahip

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r10.speaker: Seyyid Şerîf
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r10.claim: In Sharh al-Mawaqif, Sayyid Sharif calls the Moon-splitting miracle mutawatir.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r10.anchor: Şerh-i Mevâkıf’ta Seyyid Şerîf, inşikāk-ı Kamer mucizesinin mütevâtir olduğunu söylemiştir.

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r11.speaker: Sübkî
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r11.claim: Subki prefers the view that the splitting is mutawatir: it is explicit in the Qur'an and related through numerous routes in the Sahihayn and other collections.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r11.anchor: şerhinde Sübkî de bunu ihtiyar ederek der ki

ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r12.claim: Elmalılı says the Qur'an explicitly establishes the event and the combined hadith corpus is widely known enough for meaningful tawatur; because tafsir details' tawatur is disputed, those who interpret or deny the details are not declared unbelievers.
ELMALILI:54:1-8#5/r12.anchor: Tevâtürü, Kur’an’da وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ sarih olmak haysiyetiyledir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r1.speaker: İslâm âlimlerinin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r1.claim: The majority reads the moon's splitting as a miracle: at the Meccans' request, Muhammad gestured to split the moon and then reunite it; the event is called inşikaku’l-kamer or şakku’l-kamer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r1.anchor: İslâm âlimlerinin çoğunluğuna göre ayın yarıldığını belirten cümle Mekkeliler’in kendisinden bir mûcize istemeleri üzerine Hz. Peygamber’in eliyle işaret edip ayı ikiye bölmesini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r2.speaker: bu görüşü savunanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r2.claim: Those who say the event occurred during the Prophet's lifetime cite the past-tense verb, explicit reports, and the explanation in verse 2; most Muslim scholars accept this reading.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r2.anchor: âyetteki fiilin geçmiş zaman kalıbında olmasını (bunun fiilen vuku bulmuş bir durumu gösterdiğini) ve bu olayı açık biçimde tasvir eden rivayetler bulunmasını delil gösterirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r3.speaker: bu görüşü savunanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r3.claim: Another view takes the phrase as news of a cosmic change that will occur near the Resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r3.anchor: kıyamete yakın bir zamanda ortaya çıkacak kozmik bir değişikliği haber verdiğini savunanlar ise özetle şu delilleri ileri sürerler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r4.speaker: bu görüşü savunanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r4.claim: They argue that a past-tense verb can refer to the future, as elsewhere in the Qur'an, especially when certainty of a future event is stressed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r4.anchor: Geçmiş zaman kalıbındaki bu fiille gelecek zamanın kastedilmesi mümkündür. Nitekim birçok âyette bunun örnekleri mevcuttur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r5.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî ve Atâ b. Ebû Rebâh
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r5.claim: Reports attribute to Hasan al-Basri and Ata ibn Abi Rabah the interpretation that the moon's splitting is future.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r5.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî ve Atâ b. Ebû Rebâh’ın da âyeti bu şekilde yorumladıkları rivayet edilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r6.speaker: bu görüşü savunanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r6.claim: They question whether the historical event is established, citing young ages of some Companion transmitters, disputed reliability of some reports, and the lack of mutawatir transmission.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r6.anchor: bazı sahâbîlerin olayın vukuu sırasında küçük yaşta bulunmaları, bazı rivayetlerin güvenilirlik durumunun tartışılması, ayrıca konuyla ilgili hiçbir rivayetin mütevâtir haber derecesine ulaşmaması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r7.speaker: bu görüşü savunanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r7.claim: They read Anas ibn Malik's reports as saying that Muhammad showed the moon split into two, rather than reporting that it actually split.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r7.anchor: Enes b. Mâlik yoluyla gelen rivayetlerde “ayın iki parçaya ayrıldığı” değil, müşriklerin bir mûcize göstermesini istemeleri üzerine Hz. Peygamber’in de, “ayın iki parçaya ayrıldığını gösterdiği” ifade edilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r8.speaker: bu görüşü savunanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r8.claim: They argue that a spectacular event should have been seen elsewhere and entered historical or astronomical literature, but no such record exists.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r8.anchor: Böyle bir olay herkesin dikkatini çekmesi gerekirken böyle olmamış, dünyanın başka yerlerinde görüldüğü kaydedilmemiş, tarih ve astronomi literatürüne intikal etmemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r9.speaker: bu görüşü savunanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r9.claim: They connect the refusal of requested sensory miracles to the destruction of earlier deniers and to verses describing Meccan obstinacy, which says even extraordinary signs would not make them believe.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r9.anchor: daha önceki peygamberlerin toplumlarından örnekler verilip kendilerine gösterilen hissî mûcizeleri inkâr edenlerin helâk edildiklerine dikkat çekilmiş ve müşriklerce Hz. Muhammed’den istenen mûcize taleplerinin bu sebeple yerine getirilmediği belirtilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r10.speaker: gelecekteki yoruma karşı çıkanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r10.claim: They answer that a Qur'anic statement is established by the strongest proof and needs no separate mutawatir report.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r10.anchor: Kur’an’ın haber verdiği bir husus en güçlü delille sâbit olmuş demektir, dolayısıyla başka bir mütevâtir haber aramaya ihtiyaç yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r11.speaker: gelecekteki yoruma karşı çıkanlar
