KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r11.claim: They say the challenge between Muhammad and the polytheists was to produce a Qur'an like it; since the Qur'an remains a sufficient miracle until the Resurrection, this event was not a challenge requiring mass transmission.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r11.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’le müşrikler arasında meydan okuma konusu olan şey Kur’an’ın bir benzerini getirip getirememeleridir. Onlar bunda başarılı olamamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r12.speaker: gelecekteki yoruma karşı çıkanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r12.claim: They explain the lack of worldwide records by noting that the event was not announced to all humanity and was witnessed by those present around the Messenger.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r12.anchor: bu mûcize önceden bütün insanlığa duyurulmuş olmayıp o esnada görenler görmüş ve Resûlullah’ın çevresinde bulunanlar buna tanıklık etmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r13.speaker: gelecekteki yoruma karşı çıkanlar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r13.claim: They give differing horizons, cloud cover, people indoors at night, inattention, interpreting it as an eclipse, and beliefs about sorcery or spirits as reasons no wider record survived.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r13.anchor: ufukların bölgeden bölgeye farklı olması, bazı yerlerde ayın bulutlarla kaplı bulunması, gece vakti çoğu insanların meskenlerinde bulunmaları ve herkesin gözlemle meşgul olmaması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r14.claim: The future-event reading is a remote interpretation and unnecessary: rationalists who reject a past miracle would also reject a future one, while believers need no reinterpretation; miracle-demand verses describe obstinacy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r14.anchor: Bu olayın gelecekte vuku bulacağı şeklinde yorum yapmak uzak ihtimale dayalı bir te’vil olup herkesin kabul etmesini sağlama uğruna böyle bir yola girmeye gerek yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r15.speaker: Buhârî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r15.claim: The cited report in Bukhari explains that five events mentioned in the Qur'an took place in this world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r15.anchor: Buhârî’nin naklettiği rivayette açıklandığı üzere Kur’an’da geçen beş olay bu dünyada gerçekleşmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r16.speaker: bazı yorumcular
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r16.claim: Some read the phrase metaphorically as darkness parting at moonrise, using Arabic moon-based idioms for a matter becoming clear; Abu Hayyan and others reject this as unsupported.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r16.anchor: “Ayın yarılması, ay doğduğu sırada karanlığın yarılması anlamına gelir, çünkü Araplar bir konunun açıklık kazanması durumunda

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r17.speaker: Ömer Rıza Doğrul
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r17.claim: Doğrul accepts sound reports of a historical event and allows that it may have been an eclipse; symbolically, the split moon represents the fracture and doom of Arab polytheism.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r17.anchor: Son dönem müelliflerinden Ömer Rıza Doğrul’a göre konuya ilişkin rivayetler sağlamdır ve Hz. Peygamber devrinde bu olayın meydana geldiğine itiraz edilmemelidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r18.speaker: Muhammed Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r18.claim: Esed sees no reason to doubt the reports' subjective reality and considers an unusual partial eclipse causing an optical illusion a likely physical explanation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r18.anchor: Muhammed Esed’e göre de konuya ilişkin rivayetlerin sübjektif gerçekliğinden kuşkulanmak için bir sebep yoktur; gerçekte meydana gelen şeyin ise, alışılmamış optik bir yanılsamaya yol açan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r19.speaker: Muhammed Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r19.claim: Esed holds that the verse is certainly about a future event as the Last Hour approaches, whatever the event's physical nature.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r19.anchor: Fakat olayın mahiyeti ne olursa olsun âyetin ona değil, gelecekteki bir olaya, yani “son saat” (kıyamet) yaklaşırken meydana geleceklere ilişkin olduğu kesin gibidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r20.claim: The author corrects Esed's attribution to Raghib: Raghib only transmits the future-cosmic-disaster interpretation with “it has also been said,” without endorsing it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r20.anchor: Râgıb el-İsfahânî belirtilen yerde, bu görüşü bir değerlendirme yapmaksızın, “Şöyle de denmiştir ...” ifadesiyle nakletmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r21.speaker: Elmalılı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r21.claim: Elmalılı says the verse points both to a splitting in Muhammad's lifetime and to a fuller splitting as the Resurrection nears.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r21.anchor: Elmalılı âyetin, ayın hem Resûlullah döneminde yarıldığına hem de kıyamet yaklaştığında büsbütün yarılıp kıyametin kopacağına delâlet ettiğini savunur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r22.speaker: Elmalılı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r22.claim: For Elmalılı, the past splitting demonstrates that celestial bodies can break apart, making the world's end credible and warning that the Prophet's victory is near; Hasan and Ata were not denying a past event.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r22.anchor: Ayın yarılması vuku bulmuş bir olaydır; geçmişte meydana gelen bu yarılma, ayın ve onun gibi gök cisimlerinin dahi yarılıp parçalanabileceğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r23.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r23.claim: Ibn Ashur likewise treats the lunar miracle as an example of disorder in a celestial body's order, prompting reflection that the universe is finite.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r23.anchor: İbn Âşûr da bu mûcizeyle, yeryüzünün düzenini yakından ilgilendiren bir gök cismi olan ayın düzenindeki bozulmaya bir örnek gösterilip bu âlemin de sonlu olduğu üzerinde düşünme imkânı verildiği yorumunu yapar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r24.speaker: İsmail Fenni Ertuğrul
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r24.claim: Elmalılı favorably quotes Fenni's view that most scholars accept a historical miracle based on the Companions' reports and verse 2, and that believers need not doubt its occurrence or explain how it happened; Shawkani agrees.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r24.anchor: Âlimlerin ve müfessirlerin büyük çoğunluğu, ashâb-ı kirâmın rivayetlerine ve 2. âyetin açık delâletine de dayanarak Resûlullah döneminde bir mûcize olarak ayın yarılması olayının meydana geldiğini kabul etmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r25.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r25.speaker: İlyas Çelebi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r25.claim: Celebi says Ghazali, Ibn Arabi, and Shah Waliullah held that the moon did not truly split but only appeared split to observers, and criticizes this as an attempt to make the miracle easier to accept.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r25.anchor: Gazzâlî, Muhyiddin İbnü’l-Arabî ve Şah Veliyyullah ed-Dehlevî gibi sûfîlerin, ayın gerçekten yarılmış olmayıp bakanların gözüne yarılmış gibi göründüğü kanaatinde olduklarını kaydetmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r26.speaker: İlyas Çelebi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r26.claim: Celebi argues that these Sufis should instead have defended the future-splitting view attributed to Hasan and Ata, avoiding Elmalılı's objections.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r26.anchor: Kanaatimizce bunun yerine Hasan-ı Basrî ve Atâ b. Ebû Rebâh’a nisbet edilen, onun kıyamete yakın yarılacağı görüşünü savunsalardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r27.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r27.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r27.claim: The author says Celebi's attribution conflicts with Ghazali's own works, which present the event as a miracle in Muhammad's time; Ghazali also gives rational reasons why only limited reports mention it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r27.anchor: Gazzâlî hem İhyâu ulûmi’d-dîn hem el-Mustasfâ isimli eserlerinde “inşikak-ı kameri Hz. Peygamber devrinde meydana gelmiş bir mûcize olarak” takdim etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r28.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r28.speaker: Şah Veliyyullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r28.claim: Shah Waliullah calls the splitting a sign of the Resurrection rather than a miracle itself, while saying that the Prophet's foretelling it was miraculous.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r28.anchor: Şah Veliyyullah’ın bu konudaki bir ifadesi ise şöyledir: “Ayın yarılmasına gelince, bize göre bu bir mûcize olmayıp

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r29.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r29.claim: The author holds that scholars accepted the miracle's possibility without rational debate and that Qur'anic testimony need not be corroborated by other proof; because this verse is more open to interpretation and report status is disputed, no single possibility should be made a definitive article of faith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:54:1/r29.anchor: bunun yalnızca bir ihtimalini, kesin bir iman konusu olarak ele almamak gerekir. Esasen konuya ilişkin haberler üzerinde tartışma açılmasının sebebi de –hâşâ– Kur’an-ı Kerîm’e, onun mütevâtirliğine itimatsızlık değil, anlatımın farklı yorumlamaya açık durmasıdır

BURHAN:v1p73/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p73/r1.claim: Qur'anic verse endings use either identical letters or letters close in sound; examples include the matched moon and two nearly matched Fatiha endings.
BURHAN:v1p73/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر ﴾ وجميع هذه السورة على الازدواج

QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r1.claim: The invocation gives light to hearts and eyes and joy to spirits and secrets; it points to God's majesty and the perfection of His favors and kindnesses.
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r1.anchor: ' بسم الله ' كلمة بها نور القلوب والأبصار ، وبعرفانها يحصل سرور الأرواح والأسرار

QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r2.claim: Exegetes agree that the moon split during the Prophet's lifetime.
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r2.anchor: أجمع أهل التفسير على أن القمر قد انشق على عهد الرسول

QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reported seeing Mount Hira between the two halves of the moon.
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r3.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : ( رأيت حراء بين فلقتي القمر ) ولم يوجد لابن مسعود مخالف

QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r4.speaker: أنس وابن عمر وحذيفة وابن عباس وجبير بن مطعم
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r4.claim: Anas, Ibn Umar, Hudhayfa, Ibn Abbas, and Jubayr ibn Mutim also transmitted the report.
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r4.anchor: فقد روي أيضا عن أنس وابن عمر وحذيفة وابن عباس وجبير بن مطعم . . كلهم رووا هذا الخبر

QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r5.claim: The miracle has two aspects: witnesses saw it, and its concealment from those who did not see it violated what normally could not be hidden.
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r5.anchor: وفيه إعجاز من وجهين : أحدهما رؤية من رأى ذلك ، والثاني خفاء مثل ذلك على من لم يره

QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r6.speaker: أهل مكة
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r6.claim: The people of Mecca saw the split and said Muhammad had bewitched the moon.
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r6.anchor: وأهل مكة رأوا ذلك ، وقالوا : إن محمدا قد سحر القمر

QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r7.claim: The time remaining before the Resurrection is short compared with the time already elapsed.
QUSHAYRI:v3p255/r7.anchor: ومعنى { اقتربت الساعة } : أي ما بقي من الزمان إلى القيامة إلا قليل بالإضافة إلى ما مضى

BURHAN:v1p179/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p179/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p179/r1.claim: Zarkashi classifies declarative clauses as a type of sūra opening, listing al-Anbiya, al-Qamar and al-Rahman among twenty-three such sūras.
BURHAN:v1p179/r1.anchor: الرابع الجمل الخبرية نحو ﴿ يسألونك عن الأنفال ﴾ ﴿ براءة من الله ﴾

BURHAN:v3p279/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p279/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p279/r13.claim: The verse is listed as another example in the discussion of word order, without a gloss in this excerpt.

BURHAN:v1p77/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p77/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p77/r4.claim: The balanced cadence may be short, as in al-Mursalat; long, as in the battle passage; or medium-length, as in اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر.

BURHAN:v4p202/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p202/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p202/r1.claim: In a conditional divorce formula, إن لم أطلقك does not take effect until death establishes that the condition will never occur.
BURHAN:v4p202/r1.anchor: إن المشروط ب إن اذا كان عدما لم يمتنع الجزاء في الحال حتى يتحقق اليأس من وجوده

BURHAN:v4p202/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p202/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p202/r2.claim: إذا لم أطلقك makes the divorce effective immediately, because the first time without a divorce satisfies its temporal condition.
BURHAN:v4p202/r2.anchor: واذا قال اذا لم اطلقك فانت طالق تطلق في الحال لان معناه انت طالق في زمان عدم تطليقي لك

BURHAN:v4p202/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p202/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p202/r3.claim: إن normally jussives a following imperfect verb; إذا does not, since it retains a temporal sense, though it can jussive when used like إن.
BURHAN:v4p202/r3.anchor: إن إن تجزم الفعل المضارع اذا دخلت عليه واذا لا تجزمه لانها لا تتمحض شرطا

BURHAN:v4p202/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p202/r4.speaker: ابن عصفور
BURHAN:v4p202/r4.claim: One view he transmits is that إذا conveys repetition and generality: whenever Zayd rises, ʿAmr rises.
BURHAN:v4p202/r4.anchor: إن اذا هل تفيد التكرار والعموم فيه قولان حكاهما ابن عصفور احدهما نعم

BURHAN:v4p202/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p202/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p202/r5.claim: A second view says that إذا does not necessarily convey repetition or generality.
BURHAN:v4p202/r5.anchor: والثاني لايلزم قال والصحيح إن المراد بها العموم

BURHAN:v4p202/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p202/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p202/r6.claim: The author prefers generality: إذا, like other conditional nouns, means that the result follows whenever the condition occurs.
BURHAN:v4p202/r6.anchor: والصحيح إن المراد بها العموم كسائر اسماء الشرط

BURHAN:v4p202/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p202/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p202/r7.claim: أقوم إذا قام زيد links the actions immediately, while إن قام زيد only makes one's rising later; the interval may be longer.
BURHAN:v4p202/r7.anchor: اقوم اذا قام زيد فيقتضي إن قيامك مرتبط بقيامه لا يتقدم عليه ولا يتاخر عنه بل يعاقبه على الاتصال

BURHAN:v4p202/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p202/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BURHAN:v4p202/r8.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr summarizes that إن marks futurity without requiring a gap, unlike إذا, in his Mālik al-taʾwīl.
BURHAN:v4p202/r8.anchor: فالحاصل إن التقييد بالاستقبال دون اقتضاء مباعدة بخلاف اذا ذكره أبو جعفر ابن الزبير في كتابه ملاك التأويل

BURHAN:v4p202/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p202/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p202/r9.claim: Some take إذا as superfluous in إذا السماء انشقت, estimating انشقت السماء, by comparison with اقتربت الساعة and أتى أمر الله; the reply is that its apodosis is omitted.

BURHAN:v4p202/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p202/r10.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p202/r10.claim: Ibn Mālik treats إذا in 62:11 as equivalent to إذ; the author objects that this loses the sense of a continuing state that إذا supplies.
BURHAN:v4p202/r10.anchor: ورد بفوات المعنى لان اذا تفيد إن هذا حالهم المستمر

SULAMI:v2p290/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p290/r1.speaker: عبد العزيز المكي
SULAMI:v2p290/r1.claim: The Hour’s nearness indicates that most of its time has passed and the small remainder will soon pass, as the greater part already did.
SULAMI:v2p290/r1.anchor: قال عبد العزيز المكي : الاقتراب يدل على مضى الأكثر ويمضي الأقل عن قريب كما قضى الأكثر عن قريب

ITQAN:v1p78/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p78/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p78/r1.claim: The transmitted list of Medinan revelations begins with al-Baqara, Aal Imran, al-Anfal, al-Ahzab, al-Ma'ida, and al-Mumtahana, and continues through the final surah.
ITQAN:v1p78/r1.anchor: وأنزل بالمدينة سورة البقرة ثم آل عمران ثم الأنفال ثم الأحزاب ثم المائدة ثم الممتحنة

ITQAN:v1p78/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p78/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p78/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti calls the reported sequence strange and questionable, while noting that Jabir ibn Zayd was a leading scholar of the Qur'an and that al-Jaʿbari relied on the report for a revelation-order poem.
ITQAN:v1p78/r2.anchor: قلت هذا سياق غريب وفي هذا الترتيب نظر وجابر بن زيد من علماء التابعين بالقرآن وقد اعتمد البرهان الجعبري

ITQAN:v1p78/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p78/r3.speaker: البرهان الجعبري
ITQAN:v1p78/r3.claim: Al-Jaʿbari's poem places al-Qamar among the Meccan revelations, after al-Tariq in its sequence.
ITQAN:v1p78/r3.anchor: وقد اعتمد البرهان الجعبري على هذا الأثر في قصيدته

ITQAN:v1p168/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r1.speaker: حذيفة
ITQAN:v1p168/r1.claim: Hudhayfa's report says the Prophet recited al-Baqara, Aal Imran, and al-Nisa in prayer.
ITQAN:v1p168/r1.anchor: ما ثبت من قراءته صلى الله عليه وسلم لسور عديدة كسورة البقرة وآل عمران والنساء في حديث حذيفة

ITQAN:v1p168/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r2.claim: The Prophet recited al-Aʿraf in the Maghrib prayer, according to al-Bukhari.
ITQAN:v1p168/r2.anchor: والأعراف في صحيح البخاري أنه قرأها في المغرب

ITQAN:v1p168/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r3.claim: The Prophet recited al-Mu'minun in the dawn prayer and, on reaching Moses and Aaron, coughed and bowed, according to al-Nasa'i.
ITQAN:v1p168/r3.anchor: روى النسائي أنه قرأها في الصبح حتى إذا جاء ذكر موسى وهارون أخذته سعلة

ITQAN:v1p168/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r4.claim: Al-Tabarani reports that the Prophet recited al-Rum in the dawn prayer.
ITQAN:v1p168/r4.anchor: والروم روى الطبراني أنه قرأها في الصبح

ITQAN:v1p168/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r5.claim: The Prophet regularly recited al-Sajda and al-Insan in the dawn prayer on Fridays, according to al-Bukhari and Muslim.
ITQAN:v1p168/r5.anchor: روى الشيخان أنه كان يقرؤهما في صبح الجمعة

ITQAN:v1p168/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r6.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet recited Qaf in the sermon.
ITQAN:v1p168/r6.anchor: في صحيح مسلم أنه كان يقرؤها في الخطبة

ITQAN:v1p168/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r7.claim: Al-Hakim and others report that the Prophet recited al-Rahman to the jinn.
ITQAN:v1p168/r7.anchor: في المستدرك وغيره أنه قرأها على الجن

ITQAN:v1p168/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r8.claim: A sound report says the Prophet recited al-Najm in Mecca before the polytheists and prostrated at its end.
ITQAN:v1p168/r8.anchor: في الصحيح قرأها بمكة على الكفار وسجد في آخرها

ITQAN:v1p168/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r9.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet recited al-Qamar together with Qaf at the Eid prayer.
ITQAN:v1p168/r9.anchor: عند مسلم أنه كان يقرؤها مع

ITQAN:v1p168/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r10.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet recited al-Jumuʿa and al-Munafiqun in the Friday prayer.
ITQAN:v1p168/r10.anchor: والجمعة والمنافقون في مسلم أنه كان يقرأ بهما في صلاة الجمعة

ITQAN:v1p168/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r11.claim: Al-Hakim reports that the Prophet recited al-Saff to ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam when it was revealed, through to its end.
ITQAN:v1p168/r11.anchor: والصف في المستدرك عن عبد الله بن سلام أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأها عليهم حين أنزلت حتى ختمها

ITQAN:v1p168/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p168/r12.claim: The Prophet's recitation of many surahs before Companions shows that verse order within surahs was fixed by revelation; the Companions would not contradict his order, and Ibn Khuzayma says this reached mass transmission.
ITQAN:v1p168/r12.anchor: تدل قراءته صلى الله عليه وسلم لها بمشهد من الصحابة أن ترتيب آياتها توقيفي

ITQAN:v1p168/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p168/r13.speaker: الحارث بن خزيمة
ITQAN:v1p168/r13.claim: A report complicating the fixed-order argument says al-Harith brought the two closing verses of al-Tawba, testified that he heard and memorized them from the Prophet, and ʿUmar confirmed him before they were appended to the Qur'an's final surah.
ITQAN:v1p168/r13.anchor: من طريق محمد بن إسحاق عن يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه قال أتى الحارث ابن خزيمة بهاتين الآيتين

ITQAN:v1p175#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p175#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر الكوفي
ITQAN:v1p175#2/r1.claim: The transmitted order of Ubayy's codex places al-Qamar after al-Muddaththir and before al-Dukhan.
ITQAN:v1p175#2/r1.anchor: ثم المزمل ثم المدثر ثم ﴿ اقتربت ﴾ ثم حم الدخان

ITQAN:v2p435#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p435#2/r1.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v2p435#2/r1.claim: Some grammarians treat idha as extra in 84:1, reading it simply as the sky split, and compare this wording with al-Qamar's statement that the Hour drew near.
ITQAN:v2p435#2/r1.anchor: قيل قد تأتي إذا زائدة وخرج عليه

TUSTARI:54:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:54:1/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:54:1/r1.claim: In the Prophet's time the moon split into two pieces, one of which went behind Mount Hira.
TUSTARI:54:1/r1.anchor: على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلقتين، حتى ذهبت فلقة وراء جبل حراء

TUSTARI:54:1/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:54:1/r2.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
TUSTARI:54:1/r2.claim: In a sermon, Hudhayfa says the Hour is near, the world has turned away, and this life is the training ground before tomorrow's race; those who work today will win in the afterlife.
TUSTARI:54:1/r2.anchor: فقام حذيفة بن اليمان على المنبر، فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، ثم قال:

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports seeing the moon split in two at Mecca before the Prophet’s migration; people called it magic, and the verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال رأيت القمر منشقا شقتين بمكة قبل مخرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r2.speaker: أنس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r2.claim: Anas reports that Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign, whereupon the moon split twice at Mecca and the opening verses were revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p203/r2.anchor: عن أنس قال سأل أهل مكة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آية فانشق القمر بمكة مرتين

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r1.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r1.claim: Abdullah reports that the moon split during the Prophet’s lifetime; Quraysh called it his magic, but travelers confirmed seeing it, and the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p400/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقالت قريش:

FARRA:v3p96/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p96/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p96/r1.claim: The meaning is that the moon split and the Hour drew near; the order of the clauses does not alter the sense.
FARRA:v3p96/r1.anchor: والمعنى- والله أعلم- انشق القمر واقتربت الساعة، والمعنى واحد

FARRA:v3p104/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p104/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
FARRA:v3p104/r1.claim: A report says the moon split, and Ibn Masud saw Mount Hira between its two halves.
FARRA:v3p104/r1.anchor: ذكر: أنه انشق، وأن عبد الله بن مسعود رأى حراء من بين فلقتيه فلقتى القمر

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p431#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p431#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p431#2/r1.claim: He glosses the Hour’s approach as its nearness: it has drawn near.

NAHHAS:v4p285/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p285/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p285/r1.claim: Basran grammarians say the feminine tāʾ is a particle that should be silent, so it takes kasra to avoid two adjacent sukuns.
NAHHAS:v4p285/r1.anchor: هذا قول البصريين فأما قول الكوفيين فإنه لما كانت التاءات أربا

NAHHAS:v4p285/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p285/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p285/r2.claim: Kufans explain the tāʾ's sukun by the established vowels on first-, masculine second-, and feminine second-person tāʾs, leaving none for the feminine third-person form.
NAHHAS:v4p285/r2.anchor: فضمت تاء المخاطب وفتحت تاء المخاطب المذكر وكسرت تاء المخاطبة المؤنثة فلم تبق حركة فسكنت تاء المؤنثة الغائبة

NAHHAS:v4p285/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p285/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p285/r3.claim: The Hour of Resurrection is near, so people should beware lest it arrive suddenly while they persist in sins.
NAHHAS:v4p285/r3.anchor: والمعنى اقتربت الساعة التي تقوم فيها القيامة فاحذروا منها لئلا تأتيكم فجأة وأنتم مقيمون على المعاصي

NAHHAS:v4p285/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p285/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p285/r4.claim: The clause about the moon splitting is coordinated with the Hour drew near.

SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r1.claim: The majority take the moon’s splitting literally as a past event; authentic reports establish it occurred twice in the Prophet’s time.
SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r1.anchor: هذا ماض على حقيقته وهو قول عامة المسلمين، إلا من لا يلتفت إلى قوله، وقد صح في الأخبار

SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r2.claim: A view makes the past verb refer to a certain future split on Judgment Day; the author calls this contrary to consensus.
SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r2.anchor: وقيل: انشق بمعنى: سينشق يوم القيامة، فأوقع الماضي موضع المستقبل لتحققه، وهو خلاف الإجماع

SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r3.speaker: النابغة
SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r3.claim: A proposed dawn sense likens the moon’s splitting to morning breaking from darkness; al-Nābigha’s شق الصبح witnesses the usage, which the author rejects.
SAMIN-DURR:54:1/r3.anchor:
وأنشد للنابغة:
4145 فلما أدبروا ولهم دوي
دعانا عند شق الصبح داعي

ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r1.claim: Exegetes agree, and trustworthy authorities report, that the moon split during the Messenger's lifetime.
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r1.anchor: أجمع المفسرون، - وروينا عن أهل العلم الموثوق بهم - أن القمر انشق على عهد رسول الله

ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r2.claim: Zajjāj rejects the claim that the moon will split at the Resurrection: the next verse says disbelievers see a sign and turn away, which could not describe that future scene, and scholarly consensus places the event in the Prophet's time.
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r2.anchor: وزعم قوم عندوا عن القصد وما عليه أهل العلم: أن تاويله أن القمر ينشق يوم القيامة

ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r3.speaker: أنس
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r3.claim: Anas reports that Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign and he showed them the moon splitting twice; other versions from Anas say it split into two parts during his lifetime.
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r3.anchor: عن قتادة - عن أنس أن أهل مكة سألوا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - آية فأراهم القمر مرتين انشقاقه

ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r4.speaker: أنس
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r4.claim: In another Anas report, Meccans asked for a sign, the moon split twice at Mecca, and the verses about the moon and their claim of continuing magic were recited.
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r4.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة عن أنس قال: سأل أهل مكة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - آية فانشق القمر بمكة مرتين

ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r6.speaker: عبد الله
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports seeing the mountain between the two fragments of the split moon.
ZAJJAJ:v5p81/r6.anchor: قال: انشق القمر حتى رأيت الجبل بين فلقتي القمر

ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r1.speaker: عبد الله
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud says that while they were with the Prophet, one fragment went behind the mountain; the Prophet told them to bear witness.
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r1.anchor: عن أبي معمر عن عبد الله قال: انشق القمر ونحن مع النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بمعنى حتى ذهبت فرقة منه خلف الجبل

ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r2.speaker: أبو مسعود
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r2.claim: Abu Masʿud reports two fragments, one above and one below a mountain, after which the Prophet said, Bear witness.
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r2.anchor: عن أبي معمر عن أبي مسعود قال: انشق القمر على عهد النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فرقتين فرقة فوق الجبل وفرقة دونه

ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r3.claim: Ibn Umar gives the same account of the moon splitting into two parts around a mountain.
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد عن ابن عمر مثله

ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that the moon split into two visible halves and the Prophet repeatedly told them to bear witness.
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله

ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r5.speaker: جبير
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r5.claim: Jubayr reports that the moon split between two mountains; when people said Muhammad had bewitched them, someone answered that he could not have bewitched everyone.
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r5.anchor: عن محمد بن جبير عن أبيه، قال: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فرقتين على هذا الجبل وعلى هذا الجبل

ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Quran mentions three events already fulfilled, including the moon's splitting into two parts witnessed by people.
ZAJJAJ:v5p82/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ثلاث قد ذكرهن الله في القرآن قد تقضين: (اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر)

ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the moon split before the Hijra, and people saw its two parts.
ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r1.anchor: قال: قد مضى قبل الهجرة وانشق القمر حتى - رأوا شقتيه

ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r2.claim: Ikrima reports that the moon split in the Prophet's time; the polytheists cried that the moon was bewitched, and the verses were revealed in response.
ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة قال انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال المشركون سحر القمر سحر القمر

ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r3.speaker: حذيفة
ZAJJAJ:v5p83/r3.claim: In sermons at Mada'in, Hudhayfa recited the verse and said the Hour had drawn near and the moon had split; today is the training ground and tomorrow the race.

ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r1.speaker: حذيفة
ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r1.claim: Hudhayfa's sermon continues: the final goal is the Fire, and the winner is the one who reaches Paradise.

ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r2.speaker: عبد الله
ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud is reported to say that al-lizām, the great assault, the smoke, and the Romans had all already passed.
ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r2.anchor: عن مسروق عن عبد الله قال: مضى اللزام ومضت البطشة ومضى الدخان ومضى الروم

ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the moon split in the Prophet's time, with one half over Quʿayqiʿan and the other over Abu Qubays.
ZAJJAJ:v5p84/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد: انشق القمر في زمان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فكان يرى نصفه

ASAD-NOTES:54:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:intro/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:54:intro/r1.claim: Razi observes that 54:1 continues 53:57's warning that the approaching Last Hour draws nearer.
ASAD-NOTES:54:intro/r1.anchor: AS RAZI points out, the first verse of this surah appears almost like a continuation of the last verses of the preceding one, especially 53: 57

ASAD-NOTES:54:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:intro/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:intro/r2.claim: Asad infers that the two surahs were revealed around the same time, late in early prophethood, perhaps in its fourth year.
ASAD-NOTES:54:intro/r2.anchor: we may assume that both were revealed at approximately the same time, i.e., towards the end of the early part (perhaps the fourth year)

ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r1.speaker: Most commentators
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r1.claim: Most commentators identify the verse with reports from Companions that contemporaries saw the moon appear as two distinct parts one night.
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r1.anchor: Most of the commentators see in this verse a reference to a phenomenon said to have been witnessed by several of the Prophet's contemporaries

ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r2.claim: Asad accepts the reports' subjective sincerity but suggests an unusual partial lunar eclipse may have produced the optical illusion.
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r2.anchor: no reason to doubt the subjective veracity of these reports, it is possible

ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r3.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r3.claim: Asad holds that the verse does not refer to the contemporaries' reported sighting, but to a future event as the Last Hour approaches.
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r3.anchor: it is practically certain that the above Qur'an-verse does not refer to it but, rather, to a future event

ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r4.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r4.claim: The Qur'an uses past tense for future events, especially the Hour and Resurrection, to stress that their occurrence is certain.
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r4.anchor: The Qur'an frequently employs the past tense to denote the future, and particularly so in passages

ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r5.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r5.claim: Asad prefers Raghib's reading of the moon's splitting as the cosmic cataclysm ending the world before Resurrection; Zamakhshari notes support for it among early commentators, and the juxtaposition with the approaching Hour convinces Asad.
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r5.anchor: Raghib regards it as fully justifiable to interpret the phrase inshaqqa 'l-qamar ("the moon. is split asunder") as bearing on the cosmic cataclysm

ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r6.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r6.claim: Qur'anic references to the Last Hour's nearness do not follow the human concept of time.
ASAD-NOTES:54:1#n1/r6.anchor: none of the Qur'anic allusions to the "nearness" of the Last Hour and the Day of Resurrection is based on the human concept of "time"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p241/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p241/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p241/r1.claim: The author notes that many descriptions of Resurrection use passive past or present forms, dispensing with an explicit agent, including the trumpet and cosmic events.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p241/r1.anchor: ومعها سائر آيات النفخ في الصور، وكلها مبنية للعل المجهول، الماضي منها والمضارع

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p241/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p241/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p241/r2.claim: Another way the Qur'an omits the agent at the Resurrection is to attribute the event to the affected thing through a reflexive or figurative construction, as in the splitting moon and sky.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p241/r2.anchor: وإما أن يستغنى البيان القرآني عن ذكر الفاعل في موقف الآخرة، بإسناده إلى غير فاعله، مطاوعة أو مجازاً

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r1.claim: The previous sūrah's closing notice that what is near has drawn near is elaborated here as the nearness of the punishment hour.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r1.anchor: what is near has drawn near

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r2.claim: As the previous sūrah uses the stars as evidence, this sūrah presents the moon splitting as evidence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r2.anchor: the rising and setting of stars is presented as evidence over a claim

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r4.claim: The audience demanded a visible punishment sign to verify Qur’anic warnings, although the revealed Book was God's favor, able to teach, remind, and remove doubts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r4.anchor: He revealed such a Book to them that had all the necessary features to comprehensively teach and remind them and remove their doubts.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r5.claim: The Prophet is assured that the greatest signs will not make the obstinate believe because they follow desire rather than reason.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p77/r5.anchor: The greatest of signs shall not induce them to accept faith because they do not follow sense and reason

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r1.claim: Al-sāʿah means the time of Judgment and punishment warned of throughout this sūrah group, especially through 53:57; it is near and calls for preparation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r1.anchor: refers to the time of judgement and the punishment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r2.claim: Messengers warn of both a worldly punishment for persistent denial and the Hereafter's punishment; the worldly seizure is the prelude to the final one.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r2.anchor: The only difference between the two punishments is that of the beginning and the end

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r3.claim: Because the two punishments form a prelude and culmination, al-sāʿah can include both; for each nation receiving a messenger its time has drawn near, so the statement is factual, not exaggerated.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r3.anchor: Viewed thus, the time of judgement has drawn near for every nation to whom a messenger is sent.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r4.claim: The moon's splitting is a sign of the approaching punishment; God specially manifests signs during messengers' times to establish their warnings and messengerhood, as 41:53 illustrates.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p79/r4.anchor: in every nook and corner of this universe exist the signs of God’s power and wisdom

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r1.claim: The moon's splitting sign shows that the Qur’an's descriptions of cosmic upheaval are definite future events, with signs of their possibility already appearing in the world.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r1.anchor: these are definite occurrences which will happen one day

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r2.claim: A messenger's signs need not be announced miracles or challenges, nor must people have requested that particular sign; it may appear to dispel their doubts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r2.anchor: It is not necessary that a messenger present such signs as miracles; they can appear without any proclamation and without throwing any challenge.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r3.claim: Splitting the moon shows that no cosmic object, however immense, is immortal or independent: all are subject to God's command and can be destroyed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r3.anchor: none of the objects of this universe, however huge it may be, is independent or immortal

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r4.claim: In the author's view, the Qur’an and Hadith corroborate that the moon-splitting event occurred during the Prophet's lifetime; Hadith differ about its nature, not its occurrence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r4.anchor: it is evident from the Qur’ ān and corroborated by Ḥadīth in my view that such an incident did take place.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r5.speaker: some earlier authorities and some people of these times
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r5.claim: Some authorities read the verse as a future moon-splitting at Judgment Day, with past tense expressing certainty; the author rejects this as incompatible with context.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r5.anchor: Though this opinion is also ascribed to some earlier authorities and is held by some people of these times as well

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r6.claim: The future-only reading disconnects the verse from 54:2, whose visible signs are dismissed as magic; at Judgment Day disbelievers cannot make that excuse and instead acknowledge the messengers' truths, as 53:8 says.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r6.anchor: if the verse is translated thus, it will bear no relationship with the next verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r7.claim: The lack of wider historical reports does not disprove the event, since observation of such celestial events was limited to a local sphere in earlier times.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p80/r7.anchor: had such an incident taken place, it should have been mentioned in the history of other nations

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p81/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p81/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p81/r1.claim: Earlier observers lacked today's worldwide observatories and communication, so reports were local; those local witnesses were reliable, giving no reason to deny the event.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p81/r1.anchor: this sphere in itself belongs to reliable people; hence, there is no reason to deny the happening of such an event.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p81/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p81/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p81/r2.claim: He considers it probable that future lunar research will find a portion detached from and joined to another part; lack of current scientific corroboration reflects science's limits, so one should wait.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p81/r2.anchor: It is very probable that in coming times, scientists are able to investigate the moon in a more elaborate manner

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r1.speaker: حذيفة
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r1.claim: Hudhayfa reads the moon’s splitting; Ibn Jinnī treats it as an expected sign whose occurrence confirms the Hour’s nearness.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r2.claim: Ibn Jinnī says the moon’s splitting was expected as a sign of the Hour’s nearness, and its occurrence confirms that nearness.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r2.anchor: قد كان انشقاق القمر متوقعا دلالة على قرب الساعة، فإذا كان قد انشق

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r3.claim: He explains قد as an answer that marks an anticipated event as having occurred, supporting the reading’s confirmation of nearness.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p297/r3.anchor: وذلك أن "قد" إنما هي جواب وقوع أمر كان متوقعا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p257/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p257/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p257/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports seeing the moon split in two twice at Mecca before the Prophet's departure, with one half over Abū Qubays and the other over al-Suwaydāʾ; another version says Mount Ḥirāʾ was visible between the halves.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p257/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد عن أبي معمر عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال رأيت القمر منشقا شقتين مرتين بمكة قبل مخرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p257/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p257/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p257/r2.claim: Anas reports that when Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign, the moon split twice in Mecca; the account quotes the response that they would call a sign passing magic.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p257/r2.anchor: عن قتادة عن أنس قال سأل أهل مكة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فانشق القمر بمكة مرتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r1.claim: Most commentators regard Sūrat al-Qamar as Meccan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r2.claim: Another view says the sūra was revealed on the day of Badr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r2.anchor: وقيل: هي مما نزل يوم بدر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r3.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r3.claim: Maqātil says the sūra is Meccan except for three verses, beginning أم يقولون نحن and ending أدهى وأمر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: مكية إلا ثلاث آيات، أولها: أم يقولون نحن، وآخرها: أدهى وأمر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r4.claim: Quraysh demanded that the Prophet split the moon in two and promised to believe; he prayed, and it split above al-Ṣafā and Qayqaʿān on the night of Badr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r4.anchor: وسبب نزولها أن مشركي قريش قالوا للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن كنت صادقا فشق لنا القمر فرقتين، ووعدوه بالإيمان إن فعل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r5.claim: After seeing the celestial sign, Meccans said magic could not affect it; Abū Jahl proposed waiting for desert visitors, then dismissed their confirmation as magic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r5.anchor: فقال أهل مكة: آية سماوية لا يعمل فيها السحر. فقال أبو جهل: اصبروا حتى تأتينا أهل البوادي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r6.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās says one half appeared over al-Suwaydāʾ and the other over al-Ḥudaybiyya.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: شق القمر باشين، شطرة على السويداء وشطرة على الحديبية.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r7.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the moon split in Mecca twice.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r8.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās says it separated into two parts, one going away and one remaining.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r8.anchor: وعنه: انفلق فلقتين، فلقة ذهبت وفلقة بقيت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r9.claim: The opening coheres with the close of the preceding sūra: 53:57 says the approaching event has drawn near, followed here by the Hour’s nearness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r9.anchor: ومناسبة أول السورة لآخر ما قبلها ظاهرة، قال: أزفت الآزفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r10.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim witnessed the split; Ibn ʿUmar, Anas, Ḥudhayfa, and Ibn ʿAbbās also reported it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r10.anchor: وممن عاين انشقاق القمر ابن مسعود وجبير بن مطعم، وأخبر به ابن عمر وأنس وحذيفة وابن عباس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r11.claim: The narration introduces the Prophet’s response after God made the people see the moon split.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p32/r11.anchor: وحين أرى الله الناس انشقاق القمر، قال الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r1.claim: The Prophet told people to bear witness after the split; the polytheists said they had been bewitched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r1.anchor: «اشهدوا» ، وقال المشركون إذ ذاك: سحرنا محمد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r2.claim: Some polytheists said Muḥammad had bewitched them, while others said he had bewitched the moon.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r3.claim: The Muslim community rejects reading the moon’s splitting as a future event at the Resurrection; the following verse about seeing a sign and turning away requires a sign already shown.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r3.anchor: والأمة مجمعة على خلاف من زعم أن قوله: وانشق القمر معناه: أنه ينشق يوم القيامة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r4.claim: Another view says Quraysh requested a sign in general and God showed this celestial sign, one of the greatest signs because it affected the upper world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r4.anchor: وقيل: سألوا آية في الجملة، فأراهم هذه الآية السماوية، وهي من أعظم الآيات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r5.speaker: حذيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r5.claim: Ḥudhayfa reads وقد انشق القمر, presenting the split as an earlier sign that the Hour had drawn near.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r5.anchor: وقرأ حذيفة: وقد انشق القمر، أي اقتربت، وتقدم من آيات اقترابها انشقاق القمر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r6.speaker: حذيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r6.claim: In a sermon at al-Madāʾin, Ḥudhayfa said the Hour had drawn near and the moon had split during the Prophet’s era.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r6.anchor: وخطب حذيفة بالمدائن، ثم قال: إلا أن الساعة قد اقتربت، وإن القمر قد انشق على عهد نبيكم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r7.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Ḥasan’s view that the moon will split after the second trumpet at the Hour.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r7.anchor: ولا التفات إلى قول الحسن أن المعنى: إذ جاءت الساعة انشق القمر بعد النفخة الثانية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r8.claim: He also rejects the metaphorical reading that the moon’s splitting means light emerging as darkness breaks; the explanation relies on Arab comparisons of the moon with clarity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r8.anchor: ولا إلى قول من قال: إن انشقاقه عبارة عن انشقاق الظلمة عند طلوعه في أثنائها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r9.speaker: النابغة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r9.claim: Al-Nābigha’s phrase شق الصبح illustrates calling dawn’s emergence a splitting of darkness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p33/r9.anchor: قال النابغة: فلما أدبروا ولهم دوي ... دعانا عند شق الصبح داعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p49/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p49/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p49/r1.claim: He explains the moon’s split as a widening of its fissure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p49/r1.anchor: أي: أوسعت فتقها. وقرأ زهير العرقبي والأعمش

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r1.claim: The moon split apart into two portions during the Prophet's time in Mecca, about five years before the Hijra.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r1.anchor: انفصل بعضه عن بعض وصار فرقتين وذلك على عهد رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قبل الهجرة بنحو خمس سنين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r2.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r2.claim: In a sound report from Anas, the Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign and he showed them the moon split in two, with Mount Hira visible between its halves.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r2.anchor: فقد صح من رواية الشيخين وابن جرير عن أنس أن أهل مكة سألوه عليه الصلاة والسلام أن يريه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r3.claim: In reports in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, Ibn Mas'ud says one half of the moon was over the mountain and the other below it; the Prophet told people to bear witness.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r3.anchor: وفي الصحيحين وغيرهما من حديث ابن مسعود انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فرقتين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r4.claim: Another Ibn Mas'ud report says Quraysh called it magic and proposed asking travelers; travelers who arrived confirmed seeing the split, after which the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r4.anchor: ومن حديثه أيضا انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام فقالت قريش : هذا سحر ابن أبي كبشة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r5.claim: A weak report from Ibn Abbas says a group of named Meccan opponents demanded a two-part split, promised to believe, and saw the halves over Abu Qubays and Qaynuqa on the night of Badr.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74/r5.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم في الدلائل عن ابن عباس من وجه ضعيف قال : اجتمع المشركون على عهد رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r1.claim: Scholars disagree over whether the moon-splitting reports are mass-transmitted; the Sharḥ al-Mawāqif says they are, and al-Subki selects that judgment because the Qur'an states it and sound reports come by many routes.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r1.anchor: واختلف في تواتره فقيل : هو غيرمتواتر وفي شرح المواقف الشريفي أنه متواتر الذي اختاره العلامة ابن السبكي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r2.claim: Sound versions come from several Companions, including Ali, Anas, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Hudhayfa, Jubayr ibn Mut'im, and Ibn Umar; some were too young or absent to witness it, which does not invalidate the reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r2.anchor: وقد جاءت أحاديثه في روايات صحيحة عن جماعة من الصحابة منهم علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وأنس وابن مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r3.claim: The report locating the event at Mina does not conflict with Anas's report locating it at Mecca: the Prophet was then living in Mecca before the Hijra, and the Mina report does not say he was there.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r3.anchor: ولا يعارض ما صح عن أنس أن ذلك بمكة لأنه لم يصرح بأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان ليتئذ بمكة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r4.claim: A report through Mujahid and Abu Ma'mar says Ibn Mas'ud saw the moon split into two portions twice in Mecca before the Prophet's departure.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r4.anchor: من طريق مجاهد عن أبي معمر عن ابن مسعود قال : رأيت القمر منشقا شقتين مرتين بمكة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r5.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r5.claim: Ibn Hajar says the claimed consensus may concern the splitting, not its happening twice, since he knows no hadith scholar who affirmed two separate events; he suggests twice might mean two halves.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r5.anchor: قال الحافظ ابن حجر : أظن أن قوله : بالإجماع يتعلق بانشق لا بمرتين فإني لا أعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī says twice modifies Ibn Mas'ud's seeing, not the splitting: he looked away and looked again, seeing the same split, which confirms the vision without multiplying events.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r6.anchor: والذي عندي في تأويل ذلك أن مرتين في كلام ابن مسعود قيد للرؤية وتعددها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r7.claim: A report through Ata from Ibn Abbas describes Meccans rubbing their eyes and looking again before calling the split moon magic.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p74#2/r7.anchor: أخرج أبو نعيم من طريق عطاء عن ابن عباس قال : انتهى أهل مكة إلى النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī says a report of seeing the split several times can describe repeated looking rather than repeated splitting; those who looked away and looked again still saw the same event.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r1.anchor: فلوقال أحدهؤلاء رأيت القمرمنشقا ثلاث مرات على معنى الرؤية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r2.claim: The continuation of the Ibn Abbas report describes Meccans rubbing their eyes, looking again, and still seeing the moon split before calling it magic.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r2.anchor: قالوا بأبصارهم فمسحوها ثم أعادوا النظر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r3.speaker: البوصيري
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r3.claim: Al-Busiri's line about the Prophet's chest being split and the moon split for him is cited as support for a full-moon night, since the full moon is on the fourteenth.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r3.anchor: البوصيري في قوله : شق عن صدره وشق له البلد

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r4.speaker: ابن حجر الهيتمي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r4.claim: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami takes the wording al-badr rather than al-qamar to suggest the fourteenth night; al-Ālūsī knows no precedent for this and allows that al-badr means the moon generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r4.anchor: ما في قول العلامة ابن حجر الهيتي في شرحه : الظاهر التعبير بالبدر دون القمر أن الشق كان ليلة أربع عشرة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the moon was eclipsed during the Prophet's time, people called it bewitched, and the passage from this verse through 'mustamir' was revealed; eclipses most often fall on the fourteenth.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r5.anchor: ويؤيد كونه ليلة البدر ما أخرجه الطبراني وابن مردويه من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال : كسف القمر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r6.claim: There is no need to read that eclipse report as a synonym for splitting: an eclipse could have occurred together with the splitting.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r6.anchor: ولا ضرورة إلى حمل الكسوف في هذا الخبر على الانشقاق إذ لا مانع كما في البداية والنهاية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r7.claim: The two portions remained in the sky, separated briefly, and then joined; the story that the moon entered the Prophet's sleeve and came out of his garment is baseless.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r7.anchor: ثم إن القمر بعد انشقاقه لم تفارق قطعته السماء بل بقيتا فيها متباعدتين تباعدا ما لحظة ثم اتصلتا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r8.speaker: بدر الدين الزركشي عن شيخه العماد بن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r8.claim: Al-Zarkashi relates from his teacher Ibn Kathir that the sleeve story is fabricated and has no basis; the author condemns its fabricator.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r8.anchor: باطل لا أصل له كما حكاه الشيخ بدر الدين الزركشي عن شيخه العماد بن كثير

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r9.claim: The report through al-Dahhak that two moons appeared over Safa and Marwa until night is unreliable; it conflicts with sound reports by making Jews, rather than Meccan opponents, request the sign and say it was magic.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r9.anchor: وما في خبر أبي نعيم الذي أخرجه من طريق الضحاك عن ابن عباس من أنه انشق فصار قمرين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r10.claim: The popular claim that the Prophet pointed at the moon with his index finger is not found in a sound report.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r10.anchor: وقد شاع أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أشارإلى القمر بسبابته الشريفة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r11.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r11.claim: Philosophers deny the splitting because they claim rupture and reunion are impossible for celestial bodies; al-Ālūsī calls their proof flimsy and says scholars of truth have refuted it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p75/r11.anchor: وأنكر الفلاسفة أصل الانشقاق بناءا على زعمهماستحالة الخرق والالتئام على الأجرام العلوية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r1.speaker: بعض الملاحدة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r1.claim: An objector argues that a cosmic event should have been universally observed and transmitted, yet reports are concentrated among Meccans, old histories and astronomical records omit it, and the event is physically implausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r1.anchor: وقال بعض الملاحدة : لو وقعلنقل متواترا واشترك أهل الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r2.claim: The author answers that the split occurred briefly at night, when people were inattentive, and different lunar risings mean the moon was not visible everywhere at once; astronomy was also less developed.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r2.anchor: والجواب عن ذلك أنه وقع في الليل وزمان الغفلة وكان في زمان قليل ورؤية القمر في بلد لا تستلزم رؤيته

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r3.speaker: بعض الملاحدة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r3.claim: The objector further says rupture of so huge a body should make a sound vastly stronger than thunder and kill much of Earth's population.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r3.anchor: وأيضا لا يعقل لخرق هذا الجرم العظيم وأيضا خرقه يوجب صوتا هائلا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī denies that a vast sound or harm must follow and notes that unusual events can occur without known causes; the speed of sunlight illustrates that motion can be extraordinarily rapid.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r4.anchor: ومثله ذهاب التجاذب والجسام مختلفة من حيث الخواص

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r5.speaker: بعض الملاحدة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r5.claim: The objector argues that once split, the moon's pieces would lose mutual attraction and remain separated for years, as a divided mountain would.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r5.anchor: وأيضا متى خرق وصار قطعتينذهبت منه قوة التجاذب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r6.claim: The author says celestial bodies need not share Earth's properties and offers that a separated portion could remain within Earth's gravitational reach; the physical objections do not establish impossibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r6.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون إحدى القطعتين كالجبل العظيم بالنسبة إلى الأرض إذا ارتفع عنها بقاسر مثلا جذبته إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r7.claim: By way of argument, he points to unfamiliar visual phenomena, the eye's unexplained operation, and reports of the evil eye to show that people can reject effects whose causes they do not understand.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r7.anchor: على سبب الإبصار بالعين على الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r8.claim: The comparisons are dialectical concessions; ultimately God's will suffices for this miracle, and requiring a cause for every event would entail an infinite regress.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r8.anchor: وهذا كله من باب المماشاة وإلا فإراة الله تعالى كافية في الأنشقاق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r9.claim: Once possibility and God's encompassing power are established, these physical replies are unnecessary; God does what He wills.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76/r9.anchor: شمول قدرته عز وجل وأنه سبحانه فعال لما يريد

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the splitting will occur after the second trumpet blast; the past tense expresses certainty of the future event.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r1.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أنه قال : هذا الانشقاق بعد النفخة الثانية والتعبير بالماضي لتحقق الوقوع

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r2.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r2.claim: The same future interpretation is also reported from Ata.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r2.anchor: وروي ذلك عن عطاء أيضا ويؤيد الذي عليه الأكثرون قراءة حذيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r3.speaker: حذيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r3.claim: The majority's view that the event occurred before the Resurrection is supported by Hudhayfa's reading, qad inshaqqa al-qamar, 'the moon has split.'
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r3.anchor: ويؤيد الذي عليه الأكثرون قراءة حذيفة وقد انشق القمر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī follows the majority: Hudhayfa's wording is a circumstantial clause indicating that the split happened as the Hour drew near, before the Day of Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r4.anchor: فإن الجملة عليها حالية فتقتضي المقارنة لاقتراب الساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī concludes that deniers provide only improbability, not evidence of intrinsic impossibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p76#2/r5.anchor: والحاصلأنه ليس عند المنكر سوى الأستبعاد ولا يستطيع أن يأتي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r1.claim: The Hour has drawn near; it is the Resurrection.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r2.claim: When Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign, he showed the moon split in two, with Ḥirāʾ visible between the halves; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة عن أنس بن مالك أن أهل مكة سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يريهم آية فأراهم القمر شقتين حتى رأوا حراء بينهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r3.speaker: شيبان عن قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r3.claim: Shaybān's report from Qatāda says the Prophet showed the moon's splitting twice; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r3.anchor: وقال شيبان عن قتادة: فأراهم انشقاق القمر مرتين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that in the Prophet's time the moon split into two, one part above and one below a mountain, and the Prophet told them to bear witness; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرقتين، فرقة فوق الجبل وفرقة دونه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r5.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh says the moon split in Mecca; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو الضحى عن مسروق عن عبد الله قال: انشق القمر بمكة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r6.claim: Muqātil says the moon split and then came back together.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: انشق القمر ثم التأم بعد ذلك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r7.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r7.claim: In ʿAbd Allāh's report, Quraysh called the sign magic, asked travelers, and accepted their confirmation that they saw it; the verse was then revealed, with no grading stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p425#2/r7.anchor: وروى أبو الضحى عن مسروق عن عبد الله قال: [انشق القمر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r1.claim: In a surah title such as هذه هود, the word سورة is omitted from هذه سورة هود, making the title function like a tribal name.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r1.anchor: تقول هذه هود كما ترى إذا أردت أن تحذف سورة من قولك هذه سورة هود

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r2.claim: If هود itself is the surah's proper name, it is diptote like a woman named عمرو; surah names are treated like feminine names of women and lands.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r3.claim: If اقتربت is made a proper name, its initial alif becomes hamzat al-qaṭʿ, like naming a man with إضرب, so it fits noun patterns such as إصبع.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r3.anchor: اقتربت اسما قطعت الألف كما قطعت ألف إضرب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r4.claim: Titles such as نوح and الرحمن can stand for سورة نوح or سورة الرحمن; if نوح is instead a surah's proper name, it is diptote.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r4.anchor: قولهم هذه الرحمن ولا يكون هذا أبدا إلا وأنت تريد سورة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r5.claim: حم is indeclinable whether used as a surah name or annexed to it, modeled on foreign names such as هابيل and قابيل; al-Kumayt and al-Ḥammānī give poetic forms.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r6.claim: Ṭāsīn and Yāsīn follow the same non-Arabic pattern; some readers treat يس والقرآن and قاف والقرآن as foreign names followed by an implied أذكر.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r6.anchor: لا يجيء في كلامهم على بناء حاميم وياسين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r7.claim: Some readers recite يس والقرآن and قاف والقرآن by treating Yāsīn as a foreign name and supplying an implied أذكر.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r7.anchor: فمن قال هذا فكأنه جعله اسما أعجميا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r8.claim: صاد can be an Arabic-pattern surah name and then is diptote; alternatively, صاد and ياسين can be indeclinable forms fixed on fatḥa, like كيف, أين, حيث, and أمس.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r8.anchor: صاد فلا تحتاج إلى أن تجعله اسما أعجميا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r9.claim: If طسم is named as one word, change nūn to mīm and join it to Ṭāsīn, like دراب جرد and بعلبك; otherwise quote the letters unchanged.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r9.anchor: لم يكن بد من أن تحرك النون

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r10.claim: كهيعص and آلمر can only be quoted as letter names: they cannot be compounded by the models discussed or reshaped as إسماعيل because no comparable Arabic pattern exists.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r10.anchor: وأما كهيعص وآلمر فلا يكن إلا حكاية وإن جعلتها بمنزلة طاسين لم يجز

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r11.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r11.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r11.claim: نون can be declinable for speakers who decline هند, since نون can be feminine; the unknown meaning of حاميم signals its foreign origin despite Arabic-looking forms such as قابوس.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالسور)#544/r11.anchor: وأما نون فيجوز صرفها في قول من صرف هندا

BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has fifty-five verses.

BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r2.claim: A report says the unbelievers asked the Messenger for a sign, whereupon the moon split.
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r2.anchor: روي أن الكفار سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آية

BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r3.claim: Alternatively, the moon will split at the Resurrection; a reading ‘and the moon has split’ supports an already completed miracle as a sign the Hour is near.
BAYDAWI-FULL:54:1-3/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه سينشق يوم القيامة ويؤيد الأول أنه قرىء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r1.claim: The sūra completes the preceding Sūrat al-Najm by explaining the Hour's certainty and nearness, and the differing outcomes of those guided by revelation and those led by desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r1.anchor: بيان آخر النجم في أمر الساعة من تحققها وشدة قربها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r2.claim: The Prophet's confirming signs establish God's power to create and annihilate and His exclusive sovereignty; the moon's nighttime effect signals the Hour's approach and God's power to overturn the heavens.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r2.anchor: وعد بذلك بإخبار نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم وتحقق صدقه بما أيده به من آياته

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r3.claim: The sūra is named al-Qamar because the moon carries the sign of nearness foreshadowed by al-Najm; al-Inshiqāq was avoided because an unqualified splitting title would more properly suggest the sky.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r3.anchor: فلذلك سميت بما تضمنته من الاقتراب المنجم به النجم بالإشارة لا بالعبارة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r4.claim: The basmala describes God's encompassing knowledge and complete power, mercy extending to both wretched and felicitous, and perfected blessing for those He chooses.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#s054/r4.anchor: الرحمن } الذي وسعت رحمته كل شيء فعمت الشقي والسعيد

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r1.claim: The opening echoes al-Najm's closing threat that the denied Resurrection is near, while extending the preceding sūra's celestial signs from stars to the moon.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r1.anchor: لما ختمت النجم بالتهديد باقتراب القيامة التي ينكرونها بعد أن فتحها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r2.claim: The Hour is drawing very close, the moment when Resurrection occurs; little time remains relative to history since Adam because the final Prophet has come and no later community is awaited.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r2.anchor: اللحظة التي لا ساعة في الحقيقة غيرها التي تقوم فيها القيامة لأنه قل ما بقي

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r3.claim: The feminine form of the verb is itself a sign of God's immense power over the Hour.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r3.anchor: دالا على عظيم اقتداره عليها بتأنيث فعلها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r4.claim: The swift, effortless rupture of the moon is a warning sign whose extraordinary celestial effect demonstrates God's power over the coming Hour and calls people to prepare.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r4.anchor: وكانت الآيات السماوية أعظم , فاتأثير فيها أدل على تمام الاقتدار

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r5.claim: The Arabs know the lunar signs that regulate their livelihood; disrupting a celestial cause of worldly life demonstrates God's power to alter the heavenly bodies and the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r5.anchor: وكانت العرب أعرف الناس بها , دلهم على التأثير فيه على اقترابها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r6.claim: The moon's splitting was a real, famous event in the Prophet's lifetime, supported by the Qur'an and the accepted reports that make it nearly mass-transmitted.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r6.anchor: وانشقاق القمر على حقيقيته في زمان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر شهير جدا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r7.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r7.claim: Al-Qushayrī says exegetes unanimously affirm the historical splitting and cites Ibn Masʿūd's report, with no dissent from him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r7.anchor: وإجماع أهل التفسير عليه كما قاله القشيري

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وأنس
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Anas report in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections that Quraysh requested a sign and the Prophet showed the moon split, with one part on either side of Ḥirāʾ; al-Biqāʿī calls the report nearly mass-transmitted.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r8.anchor: رواه الشيخان عن ابن مسعود وأنس رضي الله عنهما

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r9.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r9.claim: Al-Qushayrī gives the occasion of revelation: Quraysh's polytheists told the Prophet to split the moon if he was truthful.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r9.anchor: قال القشيري : سبب نزولها أن مشركي العرب من قريش قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : إن كنت صادقا فشق

BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p339#2/r10.speaker: من قال المراد به سيشق
